3D Diagnostix · threeddx3 · PostgreSQL 18.3

The schema, one domain at a time

Generated from the live catalog of a database built from every file in v3/migrations/ (38 migrations). Every table, column, constraint, index, trigger, view and function below carries its own COMMENT in the database; this page quotes them. If it is here, it is in the database.

23schemas
251tables
4,176columns
787foreign keys
678check rules
1,326indexes
225rls-forced tables
70audited tables

Start here

One schema per business domain. Cross-domain links are foreign keys with a deliberate ON DELETE rule: RESTRICT where a parent must not vanish (money, history, master data), CASCADE only for true children, SET NULL only for optional links.

orders.casesThe clinical case: one or more orders for the same patient.
orders.ordersOne submission from a client.
orders.order_itemsOne service or product line. Read this before anything else.
crm.contactsWho bought it.
clinical.patientsThe pseudonymous patient; identity is elsewhere and logged.
catalog.sellable_itemsWhat can be bought.
compliance.data_classificationsWhich columns are PHI / PII, and how each is protected.

Things that will save you an afternoon

  1. Set the tenant, or see nothing. Row-level security is forced and fail-closed: with app.tenant_id unset every tenant-scoped table returns zero rows. Run SELECT core.fn_set_tenant('3ddx'); first. Human logins have it preset per database.
  2. Patient identity is not a column you can select. clinical.patient_identities is granted to owner/admin only. Use clinical.fn_get_patient_identity(patient_id, purpose); each call is written to audit.phi_access_log. For lists, clinical.v_patients_masked.
  3. Money is numeric, never float (core.money_amount = numeric(15,4)) and always sits next to a currency code.
  4. Derived values have one writer. Voucher balances, stock levels, order totals and workflow history are maintained by triggers. Write the ledger row; the balance follows.
  5. Approved records do not change. Regulated versions in state approved, superseded or migrated reject UPDATE; a correction is a new version row.
  6. Every migrated row is traceable. legacy_source + legacy_id (+ legacy_key) names the MySQL row; every row that was not migrated is in audit.migration_exclusions with a reason.
  7. Partitioned tables need their key in WHERE. comms.email_logs on sent_at; audit.audit_log, event_log and phi_access_log on occurred_at.

Classification tags

Column comments end with tags. They are flagged here and drive compliance.data_classifications, audit redaction and anonymisation. Rows of PHI columns carry a red edge, PHI-RISK an amber one.

tagcolumnsmeaning
PHI13protected health information (patient identity, DOB, clinical content)
PHI-RISK83free text or file names that may name a patient; scrubbed by anonymisation
PII79personal data about clients or staff (GDPR)
FINANCIAL68money or payment data
SECRET-REF8a reference to a secret (SSM key name, hash), never the secret
AUDIT684audit / history column
SNAPSHOT37deliberate historical copy of a value from elsewhere

Reading the chips

pk primary key · on delete restrict the parent cannot be deleted while this row exists · on delete cascade this row dies with its parent · rls forced · tenant isolation the table has RLS enabled and forced and the standard policy pol_<table>__tenant_isolation: (tenant_id = core.fn_current_tenant()) for read and write, so an unset tenant sees no rows; 223 of 225 forced tables use exactly this policy, the others list theirs · audited every change goes to the hash-chained audit log · append-only UPDATE and DELETE are rejected · traceable to legacy the table carries the legacy key trio. Constraints, indexes, triggers and policies open under each table.

core

13 tables · 157 columns · 1 views · 14 functions

Shared foundations: tenants, configuration, lookups, currencies, exchange rates, countries, business calendars, number sequences, session-context helpers.

Reference data everything else leans on: tenants (now with data_region, default currency and time zone), lookups, currencies, countries with ISO codes, business calendars (per team), number sequences. core.fn_current_tenant() lives here and is what every row-level security policy calls — unset means no rows.

core.business_calendars

AUDITV004 rls forced · tenant isolation 12 columns
Working calendars that SLAs, due dates and "business hours" are measured against: one row per calendar (e.g. Boston office, a Cairo team following US holidays, a Cairo team following Egyptian holidays). Per Q11, calendars are configured per team, not one Cairo-wide calendar; website uptime is not a calendar concern. Opening hours are in core.business_hours and holidays/one-off days in core.calendar_exceptions. Structure only: team schedules are TO CONFIRM (detailed team matrix still required), so no legacy guesses are seeded. Deactivate with is_active.

core.business_hours

AUDITV004 rls forced · tenant isolation 10 columns
Regular weekly opening hours of a business calendar: one row per working period on a weekday (a split day such as 09:00-13:00 and 14:00-18:00 is two rows). Periods of the same calendar and weekday may not overlap. Hours are wall-clock times in the calendar's time_zone; a period never crosses midnight (an overnight shift is two rows on consecutive weekdays). Child of core.business_calendars, deleted with it. Seeds must supply tenant_id (v2 seeds did not).

idbigintpkSurrogate key of the opening period.
tenant_idbigintnot null on delete restrictTenant that owns the calendar; copied from the parent calendar so row-level security can filter this table directly. FK to core.tenants (V090). · → core.tenants · default core.fn_current_tenant()
calendar_idbigintnot null on delete cascadeCalendar these hours belong to. FK to core.business_calendars. · → core.business_calendars
day_of_weeksmallintnot nullWeekday as PostgreSQL extract(dow): 0 = Sunday, 1 = Monday … 6 = Saturday.
opens_attime without time zonenot nullWall-clock time the period starts, in the calendar's time zone (inclusive).
closes_attime without time zonenot nullWall-clock time the period ends, in the calendar's time zone (exclusive).

updated_attimestamp with time zonenot nullUTC instant of the last change. Maintained by trg_business_hours__touch_updated_at. · default now()

fk_business_hours__calendar_idFOREIGN KEYFOREIGN KEY (calendar_id) REFERENCES core.business_calendars(id) ON DELETE CASCADEOpening hours belong to a calendar and are meaningless without it: deleting a calendar deletes its hours (CASCADE, configuration child with no financial or regulated content).
fk_business_hours__tenant_idFOREIGN KEYFOREIGN KEY (tenant_id) REFERENCES core.tenants(id) ON DELETE RESTRICTEvery row belongs to exactly one tenant (data owner). RESTRICT: a tenant with data cannot be deleted; tenants are retired by state, never removed.
ex_business_hours__no_overlapEXCLUDEEXCLUDE USING gist (calendar_id WITH =, day_of_week WITH =, tsrange(('2000-01-01'::date + opens_at), ('2000-01-01'::date + closes_at)) WITH &&)Two opening periods of the same calendar on the same weekday cannot overlap (the times are placed on a fixed dummy date to form a half-open range, so adjacent periods such as 09:00-13:00 and 13:00-17:00 are allowed), so business-hour arithmetic never counts a minute twice. The GiST index also serves the calendar_id FK.

core.calendar_exceptions

AUDITV004 rls forced · tenant isolation 12 columns
Dates on which a calendar departs from its weekly hours: holidays (is_working = false, e.g. US federal or Egyptian public holidays per team, Q11) and special working days (is_working = true with their own hours, e.g. Ramadan hours). One row per calendar per date; it replaces the weekly hours for that date entirely. Child of core.business_calendars, deleted with it.

core.countries

AUDITV004 traceable to legacy 14 columns
Countries 3DDX ships to, invoices or has clients in, identified by ISO 3166-1 codes. One row per country. GLOBAL reference table (no tenant_id). Legacy data has country names only; the ETL seeds the ISO list (legacy_source 'seed') and maps legacy names to these rows. Addresses, regions and ZIP time zones reference it. Deactivate, never delete.

core.currencies

AUDITV004 traceable to legacy 12 columns
ISO 4217 currencies the business prices, invoices or pays in (USD, EUR, GBP, EGP …). One row per currency, keyed by its code so money columns can carry the code directly. GLOBAL reference table: no tenant_id, shared by every tenant. Master data; deactivate with is_active instead of deleting, because prices, invoices and payments reference the code. Seeded by migration and refreshed by ETL stage 00 from legacy Currency.

symbolcharacter varying(10)Display symbol printed before amounts, e.g. '$', '€', 'E£'. Migrated from Currency.symbol. NULL = no symbol; documents print the ISO code instead.
minor_unitssmallintnot nullNumber of decimal places the currency is rounded to when an amount is finalised (2 for USD/EUR/EGP, 0 for JPY). Amounts are stored with 4 decimals (core.money_amount) and rounded to this many places on invoices. · default 2

legacy_idbigintMigrated from Currency.id (legacy numeric currency id used by Orders and price tables). NULL = currency created in threeddx3 or seeded without a legacy row.
legacy_sourcecharacter varying(64)Source of the row: 'Currency' for the legacy table, 'seed' for migration seed data. NULL = created in threeddx3.
legacy_keycharacter varying(200)Composite source key when legacy_id is not enough; not used for currencies today. NULL = the legacy_id identifies the source row.

core.exchange_rates

FINANCIALAUDITV004 audited traceable to legacy 13 columns
Daily currency conversion rates: one row per currency pair per calendar date (legacy ExchangeRate held one row per timestamp with USDEUR and USDGBP as columns; the ETL fans each source row out into one row per pair and drops duplicates of the same day). GLOBAL table: rates are market facts, not tenant data. Used to convert prices and to report in one currency; invoices copy the rate they used, so later corrections here do not change issued documents. [FINANCIAL]

core.tenants

FINANCIALAUDITV004 audited 16 columns
Data-owning organisations. One row per tenant; today only '3ddx' (3D Diagnostix), the legacy system being single-tenant, but every tenant-scoped table carries tenant_id and row-level security isolates tenants (fail-closed when no tenant is set). GLOBAL table: no tenant_id of its own, readable before a tenant is chosen so core.fn_set_tenant(slug) can resolve the slug. Soft-deleted via deleted_at; never hard-deleted while any row references it. Seeded by migration, not migrated.

Views

core.v_session_context

view 7 columns
SELECT * FROM core.v_session_context answers "what will my queries see?" before running anything that matters: tenant, acting user and role, request id, database role, and whether the session is scoped. With no tenant set, every tenant-scoped table is empty for this session.
columntypemeaning
tenant_idbigint
tenant_slugtext
acting_user_idbigint
acting_role_idbigint
request_idtext
database_rolename
tenant_scopetext
definition
 SELECT core.fn_current_tenant() AS tenant_id,
    ( SELECT t.slug::text AS slug
           FROM core.tenants t
          WHERE t.id = core.fn_current_tenant()) AS tenant_slug,
    core.fn_current_user_id() AS acting_user_id,
    core.fn_current_role_id() AS acting_role_id,
    core.fn_current_request_id() AS request_id,
    SESSION_USER AS database_role,
        CASE
            WHEN core.fn_current_tenant() IS NULL THEN 'NOT SET: tenant-scoped tables return no rows (fail-closed). Run SELECT core.fn_set_tenant(''3ddx'').'::text
            ELSE 'scoped to one tenant'::text
        END AS tenant_scope;

Functions

functionreturnsexecute granted tobehaviour
fn_add_business_hours(p_calendar_id bigint, p_from timestamp with time zone, p_hours numeric)timestamp with time zone
app_rw, owner, read
Due-date arithmetic in business time: walks the calendar forward from p_from, counting only opening hours and skipping holidays (core.calendar_exceptions), in the calendar's own time zone. fn_add_business_hours(cal, now(), 8) = one business day later. An unknown or inactive calendar falls back to wall-clock hours. Calendars are per team (Q11); seeded hours are TO CONFIRM.
fn_audit_row()triggersecurity definer trigger
owner
AFTER INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE row trigger body on audited tables: appends one hash-chained audit.audit_log row with the actor, role, database role, request id, client address, the redacted before/after images and the changed columns (touch-only updates are skipped). Serialised by the chain head row lock. app.skip_audit is honoured only for the migrator role during the bulk load.
fn_bypass_allowed(p_setting text)boolean
app_rw, owner
True when the named bypass setting (e.g. app.bypass_order_lock) is 'on' AND the session acts as the migrator role (or a superuser): the SET ROLE of the session, or its login role when none is set — evaluated the same inside SECURITY DEFINER functions. Lets the ETL and supervised corrections skip a business guard, while an application session that sets the same flag gets no bypass.
fn_current_request_id()text
app_rw, owner, read
Correlation id of the current HTTP request or job (app.request_id), or NULL. Lets an auditor join a database change to the application log line that caused it.
fn_current_role_id()bigint
app_rw, owner, read
iam.roles.id the acting person is using (app.role_id), or NULL. Recorded on status history and the audit/event logs because the requirements ask "who, in which role" for every status change.
fn_current_tenant()bigint
app_rw, owner, read
Tenant of the current session from app.tenant_id, or NULL when unset or not a number. Every row-level security policy compares tenant_id to this value, so NULL means the session sees and may write no tenant-scoped rows (fail-closed).
fn_current_user_id()bigint
app_rw, owner, read
iam.users.id of the person acting in this session (app.user_id), or NULL for system, migration and anonymous work. Feeds created_by/updated_by defaults and the audit trail.
fn_next_sequence_value(p_tenant_id bigint, p_code text)bigint
app_rw, owner
Next value of a per-tenant business number series (order numbers, case codes), created at 1 on first use. Row-locked by the upsert, so concurrent callers never receive the same number; gaps are possible when a transaction rolls back.
fn_reject_child_edit_when_parent_approved()triggertrigger
app_rw, owner
BEFORE INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE trigger body for detail rows of a versioned regulated record (protocol rows, report lines, inspection results, document record values): once the parent version is approved, superseded or migrated, its detail rows cannot be added, changed or removed. Arguments: parent table, FK column. The migrator may set app.bypass_regulated_lock to load the detail rows of migrated legacy records.
fn_reject_mutation()triggertrigger
app_rw, owner
BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE trigger body for append-only tables (history, ledgers, logs, signatures): always raises. Corrections are new rows. Attached as trg_<table>__append_only.
fn_reject_update_when_approved()triggertrigger
app_rw, owner
BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE trigger body for versioned regulated records (21 CFR Part 11 / 820): once a version's state is 'approved' it may only move to 'superseded' with no other change; approved, superseded and migrated (legacy) versions cannot be changed or deleted. Corrections insert a new version with supersedes_id. Attached as trg_<table>__immutable_when_approved.
fn_set_tenant(p_slug text)bigint
app_rw, owner, read
Scope this session to one tenant by slug: SELECT core.fn_set_tenant('3ddx'). Raises on an unknown slug instead of silently leaving the session unscoped. Returns the tenant id. core.tenants is not tenant-scoped, so the lookup works before a tenant is set.
fn_set_user(p_user_id bigint, p_role_id bigint, p_request_id text)void
app_rw, owner, read
Record who is acting in this session: user id, the role they act in, and the request correlation id. The application calls it at the start of every request, after core.fn_set_tenant.
fn_touch_updated_at()triggertrigger
app_rw, owner
BEFORE UPDATE trigger body: sets updated_at to the transaction time and, when the table has updated_by_user_id, sets it to the acting user (app.user_id) if one is set. Attached as trg_<table>__touch_updated_at to every table with updated_at.

Types and domains

typedefinitionmeaning
core.actor_kindenum: user, system, integration, anonymousWho performed an action: 'user' = a logged-in person (staff or portal user); 'system' = a scheduled job, trigger or the migration; 'integration' = an external system through its API client or webhook; 'anonymous' = an unauthenticated request (public confirmation link, unsubscribe).
core.currency_codedomain over character(3); CHECK ((VALUE ~ '^[A-Z]{3}$'::text))ISO 4217 alphabetic currency code (USD, EUR, GBP, EGP). Three capital letters; the code must also exist in core.currencies where a column has an FK.
core.email_addressdomain over citext; CHECK ((VALUE ~ '^[^@[:space:]]+@[^@[:space:]]+\.[^@[:space:]]+$'::citext))E-mail address compared case-insensitively. Format check only (one @, a dot in the domain, no spaces); deliverability is tracked in comms.email_suppressions. [PII]
core.entity_codedomain over character varying(100); CHECK (((VALUE)::text ~ '^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_.-]*$'::text))Stable machine code for a configurable thing (category, service, field, state, lookup value): lower-case ASCII letters, digits, underscore, dot, hyphen. Codes are referenced by application code and never re-used for a different meaning.
core.fdi_toothdomain over smallint; CHECK ((((VALUE >= 11) AND (VALUE <= 85)) AND ((((VALUE)::integer % 10) >= 1) AND (((VALUE)::integer % 10) <= 8))))Tooth number in FDI two-digit notation: quadrant 1-4 permanent (11-48), 5-8 deciduous (51-85); second digit 1-8 (1-5 for deciduous is enforced by the converter functions). Universal (1-32) and Palmer numbering are converted at the API edge by clinical.fn_universal_to_fdi / fn_fdi_to_universal.
core.lifecycle_stateenum: draft, active, suspended, deprecated, archivedLifecycle of configurable master data: 'draft' = being prepared, not selectable; 'active' = in use; 'suspended' = temporarily unavailable, history intact; 'deprecated' = no new use, existing references valid; 'archived' = retained for history only.
core.money_amountdomain over numeric(15,4)Monetary amount with four decimal places (enough for unit prices and exchange-rate conversion before rounding to cents). Signed: sign rules (non-negative prices, negative credits) are CHECKs on each column. Always paired with a currency on the same row or a stated source of the currency. [FINANCIAL]
core.rate_percentdomain over numeric(7,4); CHECK (((VALUE >= (0)::numeric) AND (VALUE <= (100)::numeric)))Percentage expressed 0-100 with four decimals (12.5 = 12.5 %). Used for discounts and allocation shares; tax rates use a 0-1 fraction instead.
core.sha256_hexdomain over character(64); CHECK ((VALUE ~ '^[0-9a-f]{64}$'::text))SHA-256 digest as 64 lower-case hexadecimal characters: content hashes of files and regulated records, audit chain hashes, token hashes.

iam

16 tables · 190 columns · 1 functions

Identity and access: staff and portal user logins, employees, teams/departments, roles, capabilities, password policy, sessions, API clients, staff relationships, work schedules.

Who logs in. iam.users holds staff, portal (client), integration and system parties, told apart by party_kind. No legacy password was migrated: every migrated user has password_hash NULL and must_change_password true. New in v3: password history, staff relationships (legacy WSacountsPairs) and work schedules.

iam.password_history

SECRET-REFV006 rls forced · tenant isolation append-only 6 columns
Previous password hashes of a user, kept only to refuse re-use of recent passwords (password policy, D2 G2 / C02). iam.user_sessions

PIISECRET-REFV006 rls forced · tenant isolation audited 9 columns
Live sign-in sessions issued by threeddx3: one row per session token, with expiry and revocation. Deliberately empty after migration: legacy UserSessions recorded no expiry, so carrying its 492,820 tokens would have created credentials with an authority the source never gave them (decision recorded in stage_10 and audit.migration_exclusions); last-seen times went to iam.users.last_login_at instead. Only a hash of each token is stored. Expired rows are purged by a job. Contains PII.

iam.users

PIISECRET-REFAUDITV006 rls forced · tenant isolation audited traceable to legacy 29 columns
One login identity: a staff user (legacy WSacounts, party_kind 'employee'), a portal user of a client account (legacy UserAcounts, 'client'), a machine identity acting through the API ('integration') or the system itself ('system'). Owned by the identity module; staff HR attributes are in iam.employees, the client account behind a portal user is crm.contacts.user_id. Soft-deleted (deleted_at); never hard-deleted while history references it. Holds only one-way password hashes: legacy passwords were reversibly encrypted and are not migrated (U3), so migrated users have no password and must reset. Contains PII.
columntypetags · constraintsmeaning
idbigintpkSurrogate key of the login identity; referenced by every actor column (created_by_user_id, author_user_id …) across the database.

A person who is both staff and a client has two rows, as in legacy.

Migrated from WSacounts.Email / UserAcounts.Email; legacy rows without a usable address get ws<id>@legacy.3ddx.internal or user<id>@legacy.3ddx.internal, and duplicates are prefixed with the legacy id so the unique key holds. [PII]

Set by the application when the user chooses a password. NULL = no password set: the user cannot log in with a password and must use the reset flow; true for every migrated user (legacy passwords are not migrated, U3) and for integration/system identities that never use a password. [SECRET-REF]

iam.work_schedules

AUDITV006 rls forced · tenant isolation traceable to legacy 17 columns
Recurring weekly working hours of a staff user or of a whole team (D4 gap 2; legacy UserAccounts getSchedule / updateSchedule and the CP planner). One row per working slot on one weekday within a validity range; several slots a day (split shifts) are allowed but may not overlap. Used for task assignment and SLA planning alongside the team's business calendar (core.business_calendars, holidays). Superseded schedules are closed with valid_to.

app_rw, owner
Login gateway: returns the account(s) for an e-mail across tenants, with the password hash to verify, before any tenant is set (iam.users is under fail-closed RLS). SECURITY DEFINER owned by threeddx3_owner; executable by the app role only. The caller must record the outcome with audit.fn_log_event('login_success'|'login_failure', …). Migrated users have no hash and must_change_password = true: they log in only through a reset (user decision U3).

crm

18 tables · 300 columns · 1 functions

Clients and prospects: contacts (doctors, scanning centres, DSOs), addresses, phones, emails, relationships, preferences, leads, campaigns, special requests, equipment, feedback, sales targets.

The customer side. A crm.contacts row is the doctor, scanning centre or DSO you invoice and ship to; the iam.users row is who logs in. v3 decodes the legacy doorType bitmask into named booleans, adds typed phones, equipment, competitors, feedback, sales targets and special-request categories. One placeholder “Unknown client” per tenant owns orders whose legacy doctor account no longer exists.

crm.contacts

PHI-RISKPIIFINANCIALAUDITV007 rls forced · tenant isolation audited traceable to legacy 45 columns
A client or business party 3DDX deals with: a doctor or dental practice, a scanning centre submitting on behalf of doctors, a DSO (dental service organisation) grouping practices, a clinic, distributor, partner lab or other party. One row per account: migrated from legacy UserAcounts (doctors and scanning centres) and third_parties (partners), plus one placeholder "Unknown client" per tenant owning the orders whose legacy DocID has no account (U7). Orders, price lists, vouchers and invoices reference it with RESTRICT, so contacts are soft-deleted (deleted_at), never removed. Contains PII.

catalog

12 tables · 190 columns

What 3DDX sells: categories, sellable items (services, products, licences), order-form fields with conditional rules, upload requirements, teeth-chart components.

Everything a client can buy, in one table: catalog.sellable_items. Order-form fields carry conditional rules (item_field_rules) and per-item upload requirements; the dynamic teeth chart is described by tooth_chart_components.

catalog.item_field_rules

AUDITV008 rls forced · tenant isolation traceable to legacy 16 columns
Conditional order-form rules (D3 §X5): a field on an item's form becomes visible, required, or limited to a subset of its options depending on other answers or on order-line attributes such as Digital vs Physical. Examples: Screw Type required only when Kind of Implant = OEM; Gingiva Shade options filtered by Gingiva Shade System (Vita / Ivoclar / Other -> text required); Abutment options filtered by Retention. One row = one rule on one item_fields placement. Evaluation (V100, server side, re-run on submit): for 'visible' and 'required' the field is visible / required when any active rule of that kind holds, and falls back to always-visible / item_fields.is_required when it has no active rule of that kind; for 'options' the first active rule that holds (by sort_order) limits the options, and with none holding all active options are offered. Configuration child of catalog.item_fields.
columntypetags · constraintsmeaning
idbigintpkSurrogate key of the conditional form rule; not referenced elsewhere.
tenant_idbigintnot null on delete restrictOwning tenant (core.tenants; FK added by V090); always the tenant of the item field. Row-level security isolates rows by this column. · → core.tenants · default core.fn_current_tenant()
item_field_idbigintnot null on delete cascadeThe field placement (field on one sellable item's form) the rule controls. · → catalog.item_fields
rule_kindcharacter varying(20)not nullWhat the rule controls: 'visible' = the field is shown only while the condition holds; 'required' = the field must be answered while the condition holds; 'options' = while the condition holds only option_codes are offered.
conditionjsonbnot nullWhen the rule applies, as a JSON object over other answers on the same form. Shape: a leaf {"field": "<catalog.fields.code>", "op": "<op>", "value": <scalar>} or {"field": ..., "op": "in"|"not_in", "values": [<scalar>, ...]}, where op is one of eq, ne, in, not_in, is_set, is_not_set, gt, gte, lt, lte and a select answer is compared by option code; a leaf may name an order-line attribute instead of a field: {"attribute": "is_digital", "op": "eq", "value": true}; combinators {"all": [<cond>, ...]}, {"any": [<cond>, ...]}, {"not": <cond>}. {} = always holds. Validated by the V100 evaluator; only the object type is checked here. · default '{}'::jsonb
option_codescharacter varying(100)[]For rule_kind = 'options': the codes (catalog.field_options.code of the controlled field) offered while the condition holds. Codes rather than ids so seeds are portable between environments; membership is validated by V100. NULL = not an options rule.
sort_orderintegernot nullEvaluation order among 'options' rules of the same field placement, ascending; the first that holds wins. · default 0
is_activebooleannot nullFalse = rule switched off without deleting it (kept for review of which rule applied to old cases). · default true
notestextWhy the rule exists, e.g. the requirement document and user story it implements. NULL = no note.
legacy_idbigintSource row id when loaded from a legacy source. NULL = created in threeddx3 (seeded or configured).
legacy_sourcecharacter varying(64)Source of a loaded row, e.g. 'ec2:<path>' for a JSON form definition. NULL = created in threeddx3.

catalog.sellable_items

AUDITV008 rls forced · tenant isolation audited traceable to legacy 26 columns
Everything 3DDX sells: a service (design, planning, production per case), product (printer, resin, kit), licence, rental or bundle. One row = one sellable item of one tenant. Legacy Services (one row per service and order type: a temporary and a final crown, or a crown on a restoration vs an appliance order, are different services — v2 defect 48), product_details (3D printers and accessories) and the price dimensions of the wide UserAcounts price book migrate here. Owned by the catalog module; referenced by order items, shopping carts, bundles, pricing lists, formulas, tiers and rules. Lifecycle by state (never deleted once ordered).

AUDITV008 rls forced · tenant isolation 7 columns
Pairs of teeth-chart components of one service that cannot be selected on the same tooth (D3 §12): e.g. Pontic conflicts with Crown and with Abutment, while Crown and Abutment may share a tooth (no row). Types and domains

typedefinitionmeaning
catalog.fulfilment_kindenum: production, inventory, licensing, rental, manual, noneHow an item is delivered: 'production' = made per order by production; 'inventory' = picked from stock; 'licensing' = a licence is issued; 'rental' = a unit is lent and returned; 'manual' = handled outside the system; 'none' = nothing to deliver (fees).
catalog.item_kindenum: service, product, license, rental, bundleWhat a sellable item is: 'service' = design/planning/production work done per case; 'product' = a physical good from stock (printer, resin, kit); 'license' = software entitlement; 'rental' = loaner equipment with a return; 'bundle' = a package of other items.

pricing

8 tables · 156 columns · 4 functions

What it costs: tenant-default and client price lists, tiers, rules, and the formula engine that keeps per-arch / per-implant guide pricing as rules.

Price lists (tenant default from legacy uID 0, client lists), tiers, rules and the formula engine that keeps per-arch / per-implant guide pricing as data. pricing.fn_quote_total explains any price; quote_lines records what was quoted.

AUDITV009 rls forced · tenant isolation traceable to legacy 16 columns
Conditions on order-line attributes. pricing.formula_terms

FINANCIALAUDITV009 rls forced · tenant isolation audited traceable to legacy 21 columns
The terms of a pricing formula; the line price is their sum, evaluated in sequence by pricing.fn_quote_line (per arch when the formula applies per arch). One row = one term: a base rate, a rate x quantity (optionally capped), a rate chosen by quantity from a scale, a flat amount, or a percentage of the terms before it. Configuration child of pricing.formulas.
columntypetags · constraintsmeaning
idbigintpkSurrogate key. Referenced by pricing.formula_conditions.term_id.
tenant_idbigintnot null on delete restrictOwning tenant (core.tenants; FK added by V090); always the tenant of the formula. Row-level security isolates rows by this column. · → core.tenants · default core.fn_current_tenant()
formula_idbigintnot null on delete cascadeThe formula this term belongs to. · → pricing.formulas
sequencesmallintnot nullEvaluation order within the formula, ascending from 1; a 'percent' term applies to the running total of the terms before it. · default 1
term_kindcharacter varying(20)not nullHow the term contributes: 'base' = one rate, once; 'per_unit' = rate x quantity; 'per_unit_capped' = rate x least(quantity, cap_quantity) (e.g. per implant, capped at six); 'scale' = one rate chosen by the quantity (scale_code_prefix + zero-padded quantity, e.g. implant_site_07); 'flat' = flat_amount, no rate lookup; 'percent' = percent_value % of the terms before it.
rate_item_codecore.entity_codecatalog.sellable_items.code whose rate in the quoted price list (pricing.price_list_items) supplies the number, so the rate stays per client and currency. Required for base / per_unit / per_unit_capped. NULL = scale, flat or percent term.
scale_code_prefixcore.entity_codeFor 'scale' terms: the rate code is this prefix plus the two-digit quantity (implant_site_ + 07 -> implant_site_07, legacy impSiteUSD_7). NULL = not a scale term.
quantity_sourcecharacter varying(30)not nullWhich quantity the term multiplies or scales by, read from the quote's quantities (suffixed _maxilla / _mandible for per-arch formulas): 'unit' = once (never looked up); 'implant_count'; 'crown_count'; 'abutment_count'; 'pontic_count'; 'veneer_count' and 'inlay_onlay_count' (v3: teeth-chart components); 'arch_count'; 'tooth_count'; 'aligner_count'; 'page_count'; 'quantity' = the ordered quantity. · default 'unit'::character varying
cap_quantityintegerUpper bound on the quantity for 'per_unit_capped' terms (e.g. 6 implants). NULL = no cap (required for per_unit_capped).

pricing.formulas

AUDITV009 rls forced · tenant isolation audited traceable to legacy 21 columns
How a formula-priced item (pricing_method = 'formula', the classic surgical-guide price book, Q4) combines rates into a line price, e.g. per arch: base by (software, guide type, kit, scanning appliance) + per-implant rate x implant count capped at six. One row = one formula for an item or a whole category; pricing.fn_select_formula picks the active one whose conditions all hold, lowest priority first. The rates themselves stay per client in pricing.price_list_items. Seeded (V2nn) from ordersCostCalculationFunctions.php; configuration, deactivated rather than deleted.

pricing.price_list_items

FINANCIALAUDITV009 rls forced · tenant isolation audited traceable to legacy 18 columns
The rates: one row = the price of one sellable item, one priced field (optionally for one item), or one article in one price list (about 8.7M migrated rows, most from ServiceFieldsPrices). An item's list price = its own row + the rows of each priced field selected; formula-priced items read their rates here through formula_terms.rate_item_code. Legacy split every price into a digital (design-only) and a manufacturing component; both are kept. Currency = the list's currency_code. Edited in place; history of charged amounts lives in pricing.quote_lines and billing.

pricing.price_lists

FINANCIALAUDITV009 rls forced · tenant isolation audited traceable to legacy 19 columns
A price book in one currency: either a tenant-wide default or one client's (or partner's, or campaign's) overrides. One row = one list; its rates are pricing.price_list_items. Resolution for a client order: the client's active list in the order currency first (priority 10), then the tenant defaults (priority 100) for anything the client list does not price (Q5). Legacy sources: FieldsDefaultPrices / SGServicesDefaultPrices (default), UserAcounts.uID = 0 rows (tenant_default), SGServicesPrices / ServiceFieldsPrices / the wide UserAcounts price columns (client). Lists are deactivated or end-dated, not deleted, once used for a quote.

pricing.quote_lines

FINANCIALAUDITSNAPSHOTV009 rls forced · tenant isolation audited traceable to legacy 18 columns
Why an order item cost what it cost: the price breakdown resolved when the item was priced — base rate, priced fields, tier, formula terms, rush fee, discounts, surcharges, voucher credit, manual adjustment. One row = one component of one order item's price; the item's line total is the sum of line_amount. Makes historical prices explainable after price lists change (legacy could not explain a past total). Financial: kept with the order item (RESTRICT). TO CONFIRM: whether lines become immutable once the item is charged (then an immutability trigger is added in V110); until then a re-price replaces the item's lines.

orders

20 tables · 389 columns · 7 functions

Cases, orders and order items with their field values, status history, comments, locks, decisions, confirmation links, dependencies, assignments, AI-planning state and carts.

The centre of the system, now with a level above the order. orders.cases groups the orders of one clinical case (split-arch orders can share one; migrated orders get one case each, with pairing candidates queued for review). orders.order_items is one line; parent_item_id and item_role express iSmile sub-orders and temporary / final restorations. Decisions, confirmation links, dependencies, assignments and Relu AI-planning state are new tables.

orders.case_pairing_candidates

PHI-RISKPIIAUDITV011 rls forced · tenant isolation 15 columns
Review list of order pairs that may be one split-arch case but whose evidence was ambiguous (Q3, U8). One row per unordered pair of orders (order_a_id < order_b_id). Written by the ETL pairing step and later by a pairing job; a person accepts (the orders are then moved under one case with pairing_method = 'manual') or rejects. Unambiguous pairs never appear here; they are linked directly. Contains PII.

orders.cases

PHI-RISKPIIAUDITV011 rls forced · tenant isolation traceable to legacy 16 columns
Clinical case above one or more orders (Q3: no legacy case id exists). One row per case: a single order is a one-order case; a split-arch submission (one order per arch) becomes two orders under one case. Every order belongs to exactly one case (orders.orders.case_id). Historical pairs are auto-linked by the ETL only when the evidence is unambiguous; ambiguous pairs stay in separate single cases and are listed in orders.case_pairing_candidates for review (U8). orders.order_item_decisions

PHIPHI-RISKAUDITV011 rls forced · tenant isolation append-only 18 columns
Append-only record of client decisions at approval gates (digest 03 X4): design/try-in/Ti bar/Zirconia confirmation or amendment request (Final AoX, FMP), redo try-in, post-ship adjustment, Relu AI plan actions (FT session, amendment, proceed with guide fabrication), iSmile doctor confirmation. One row per decision with who (doctor contact or staff user), how (channel), when, notes and the exact file approved. A regulated record (21 CFR Part 11 design approval, V3_DESIGN C6): rows are never updated or deleted; a correction is a new row with supersedes_id. Idempotent: the same idempotency key cannot record twice. Contains PHI-risk free text.
columntypetags · constraintsmeaning
idbigintpkSurrogate key of the decision; system-generated.
tenant_idbigintnot null on delete restrictTenant that owns the item; row-level security scope. · → core.tenants · default core.fn_current_tenant()

workflow_state_idbiginton delete restrictGate state the item was in when the decision was made (workflow.workflow_states, is_approval_gate). NULL = decision not taken at a workflow gate (e.g. Relu clinic actions on the AI plan dashboard). · → workflow.workflow_states
decision_kindcharacter varying(40)not nullWhat was decided: 'confirmed' = client approves the design/try-in/product/plan as sent; 'amendment_requested' = client asks for changes (notes required); 'redo_try_in' = try-in must be remade (AoX); 'proceed_with_minor_adjustments' = proceed to Ti bar/Zirconia with minor adjustments (AoX); 'post_ship_adjustment_requested' = adjustment requested after shipping, item returns to QC (AoX); 'ft_session_requested' = fine-tuning session booked on the Relu AI plan; 'proceed_guide_fabrication' = proceed with guide fabrication from the Relu AI plan. List TO CONFIRM as further gates are specified.
channelcharacter varying(20)not nullHow the decision reached 3DDX: 'email_link' = confirmation link in an e-mail (confirmation_link_id); 'connect' = Connect portal popup or button; 'cp' = entered in CP by staff; 'verbal' = told to staff by phone or in person and recorded by them; 'api' = an integration partner.
notestextPHI-RISKClient's notes with the decision (optional for confirmations, required for amendment requests; Relu caps amendment text at 2000 characters in the UI). Printed in internal history; may name the patient. NULL = no notes. [PHI-RISK]

confirmation_link_idbiginton delete restrictConfirmation link used (orders.confirmation_links); each link records at most one decision. NULL = decision not made through an e-mail link. · → orders.confirmation_links
subject_document_idbiginton delete restrictExact file version approved or rejected (docs.documents: HTML review, design STL). NULL = the decision is not about a specific file. · → docs.documents

content_hashcore.sha256_hexSHA-256 of the canonical decision content at recording time, referenced by compliance.electronic_signatures when the decision is signed. NULL = no signature-grade hash taken (e.g. migrated or verbal decisions).

orders.order_items

PHIPHI-RISKFINANCIALAUDITSNAPSHOTV011 rls forced · tenant isolation audited traceable to legacy 54 columns
One service or product line on an order: a surgical guide, treatment plan, report, temporary or final restoration, GFMR, FMP, iSmile sub-order or refinement, software licence, appliance, misc charge. Replaces legacy OrderSG, OrderTP, OrderRestoration, OrderSoftware, OrderMisc, OrderOther, OrderAppliance, OrderSim and SubOrderServices (legacy_source says which). Items form a hierarchy through parent_item_id (iSmile sub-orders under the iSmile item, refinements under the treated item). Execution state lives in workflow.workflow_instances; status here is the client-facing summary. Soft-deleted; price columns are frozen once invoiced (V110). Contains PHI (service_notes).

idbigintpkSurrogate key of the order item; system-generated.

NULL = top-level item (always for 'primary'). · → orders.order_items
item_rolecharacter varying(40)not nullRole of the line within its case: 'primary' = a top-level service or product ordered on its own; 'ismile_suborder' = one aligner stage under an iSmile treatment item; 'refinement' = an iSmile refinement of an earlier treatment; 'temp_restoration' = the temporary restoration of a restoration pair; 'final_restoration' = the final restoration of a restoration pair; 'addon' = an extra service attached to another item (e.g. IOS model auto-created with an SG). Set by the ETL from the legacy hierarchy (Q21) and by the ordering flows. · default 'primary'::character varying
restoration_stagecharacter varying(20)For restoration items, which stage the line delivers: 'temporary' = interim prosthesis; 'final' = definitive prosthesis. Required to match item_role for temp/final restoration roles; may also be set on a primary standalone restoration. NULL = the item is not a restoration.
sellable_item_idbigintnot null on delete restrictCatalogue item sold on this line (catalog.sellable_items); its code includes the order type. · → catalog.sellable_items

NULL = not on hold, or a migrated hold whose type legacy did not record.

ck_order_items__amounts_non_negativeCHECKCHECK (((legacy_id IS NOT NULL) OR (((unit_price)::numeric >= (0)::numeric) AND ((discount_amount)::numeric >= (0)::numeric) AND ((voucher_amount)::numeric >= (0)::numeric) AND ((line_total)::numeric >= (0)::numeric) AND ((commission_amount IS NULL) OR ((commission_amount)::numeric >= (0)::numeric)))))For lines created in threeddx3, unit price, discount, voucher credit, line total and commission are never negative. Migrated lines (legacy_id set) are exempt because legacy cost columns were unvalidated doubles. Field surcharges may be negative (an option that lowers the price) - TO CONFIRM.

ck_order_items__hold_typeCHECKCHECK (((hold_type IS NULL) OR ((hold_type)::text = ANY ((ARRAY['customer'::character varying, 'internal'::character varying])::text[]))))Hold type is customer or internal when set.
ck_order_items__item_roleCHECKCHECK (((item_role)::text = ANY ((ARRAY['primary'::character varying, 'ismile_suborder'::character varying, 'refinement'::character varying, 'temp_restoration'::character varying, 'final_restoration'::character varying, 'addon'::character varying])::text[])))Item role is primary, ismile_suborder, refinement, temp_restoration, final_restoration or addon.
ck_order_items__not_own_parentCHECKCHECK (((parent_item_id <> id) AND (redo_of_item_id <> id)))An item cannot be its own parent or remake itself.
ck_order_items__parent_matches_roleCHECKCHECK (((((item_role)::text <> ALL ((ARRAY['ismile_suborder'::character varying, 'refinement'::character varying])::text[])) OR (parent_item_id IS NOT NULL)) AND (((item_role)::text <> 'primary'::text) OR (parent_item_id IS NULL))))iSmile sub-orders and refinements always hang under a parent item; a primary item never does.
ck_order_items__quantity_positiveCHECKCHECK ((quantity > (0)::numeric))Quantity is strictly positive.
ck_order_items__restoration_stageCHECKCHECK (((restoration_stage IS NULL) OR ((restoration_stage)::text = ANY ((ARRAY['temporary'::character varying, 'final'::character varying])::text[]))))Restoration stage is temporary or final when set.
ck_order_items__role_matches_restoration_stageCHECKCHECK (((((item_role)::text <> 'temp_restoration'::text) OR ((restoration_stage)::text = 'temporary'::text)) AND (((item_role)::text <> 'final_restoration'::text) OR ((restoration_stage)::text = 'final'::text))))A temporary-restoration item has stage temporary; a final-restoration item has stage final.
ck_order_items__statusCHECKCHECK (((status)::text = ANY ((ARRAY['draft'::character varying, 'submitted'::character varying, 'pending_information'::character varying, 'in_review'::character varying, 'confirmed'::character varying, 'in_design'::character varying, 'awaiting_approval'::character varying, 'in_production'::character varying, 'quality_check'::character varying, 'ready_to_ship'::character varying, 'shipped'::character varying, 'delivered'::character varying, 'completed'::character varying, 'on_hold'::character varying, 'cancelled'::character varying, 'not_indicated'::character varying])::text[])))The item summary status is one of the sixteen client-facing values.
ck_order_items__total_consistentCHECKCHECK (((line_total)::numeric = (((((unit_price)::numeric * quantity) + (fields_amount)::numeric) - (discount_amount)::numeric) - (voucher_amount)::numeric)))Line total always equals unit price x quantity + field surcharges - discount - voucher credit.
ck_order_items__zero_charge_has_reasonCHECKCHECK (((legacy_id IS NOT NULL) OR ((line_total)::numeric <> (0)::numeric) OR (zero_charge_reason_id IS NOT NULL)))A line created in threeddx3 whose total is zero must say why (zero-cost reason: voucher, redo, other - Final AoX US#32). Migrated lines (legacy_id set) are exempt: legacy never recorded a reason for most free lines, so the rule cannot hold for history.

Functions

functionreturnsexecute granted tobehaviour
fn_assign_order_number()triggertrigger
app_rw, owner
BEFORE INSERT on orders.orders: assigns the next per-tenant order number when none is given. Migrated orders keep their legacy Orders.ID as order_number; the sequence is moved past the legacy maximum by the ETL so new numbers never collide.
fn_recalculate_item_total()triggertrigger
app_rw, owner
BEFORE INSERT/UPDATE on orders.order_items: line_total = unit_price × quantity + fields_amount − discount_amount − voucher_amount (the rule ck_order_items__total_consistent asserts). On update, fields_amount is re-summed from the item's field values unless the update itself carries a new fields_amount (pushed by fn_refresh_item_fields_amount).
fn_recalculate_order_total()triggertrigger
app_rw, owner
AFTER INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on orders.order_items: recomputes the order's subtotal, discount, voucher and total from its live (not soft-deleted) items, keeping the order-level adjustment. total = subtotal − discount − voucher + adjustment, as ck_orders__total_consistent asserts. Skipped for the migrator when app.bypass_totals is on (bulk load; stage 90 recomputes all totals).
fn_refresh_item_fields_amount()triggertrigger
app_rw, owner
AFTER INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on orders.order_item_field_values: re-sums the item's field surcharges into order_items.fields_amount, which in turn recalculates line_total and the order totals. v2 recalculated only when the item itself changed, so surcharges loaded after their item (as the ETL does) never reached the total. The migrator may set app.bypass_totals during the bulk load; stage 90 then recomputes all totals in one pass.
fn_reject_financial_edit()triggertrigger
app_rw, owner
BEFORE UPDATE/DELETE on orders.order_items. Replaces the legacy prevent_update_invoiced_* trigger family: once an item is invoiced or has any billing.charges row (a charge row exists only once money was taken), its price, quantity, currency, discount, voucher amount, billability, item sold and zero-charge reason are frozen and it cannot be deleted or soft-deleted. Status, dates and assignments stay editable so production continues. Deliberate divergence from legacy: legacy silently reverted the edit; v3 raises.
fn_reject_party_edit_when_invoiced()triggertrigger
app_rw, owner
BEFORE UPDATE on orders.orders: once any item is invoiced or charged, the doctor (contact_id), scanning centre and patient of the order are frozen — the legacy rule behind "prevent sending charged orders to another billed account" (prevent_update_invoiced_orders_ctbb_credit).
fn_reject_when_locked()triggertrigger
app_rw, owner
BEFORE UPDATE on orders.orders and BEFORE INSERT/UPDATE on orders.order_items: rejects the change while another holder has an active, unexpired lock on the order. The user who holds a user lock may edit; system locks (charging, invoicing) block everyone. Legacy enforced this only in PHP, so background jobs could write to a locked order. The migrator may bypass with app.bypass_order_lock.

Types and domains

typedefinitionmeaning
orders.lock_sourceenum: user, systemWho took an order lock: 'user' = a staff member opened the order for editing; 'system' = a process (charging, invoicing) locked it.
orders.lock_statusenum: active, released, expiredOrder lock state: 'active' = held, edits by others rejected; 'released' = closed by its holder; 'expired' = timed out and released by the system.

clinical

17 tables · 281 columns · 1 views · 5 functions

Clinical data: pseudonymous patients with a separately protected identity, tooth charts and sites, implant systems, sleeves, fixation pins, surgical kits and their drilling protocols, shades.

Patient and tooth-level data, split for PHI. clinical.patients is pseudonymous (a system patient_code, no name); the name, date of birth and sex live 1:1 in clinical.patient_identities, which no application or read role can select. Read identity through clinical.fn_get_patient_identity / fn_list_patient_identities (each call is logged in audit.phi_access_log) or the masked view clinical.v_patients_masked. Surgical kits and their versioned protocols, guide sleeves and fixation pins also live here.

clinical.guide_fixation_pins

AUDITSNAPSHOTV010 rls forced · tenant isolation traceable to legacy 19 columns
Fixation pins (and their pin sleeves) selected for a surgical guide order item: which manufacturer's pin/sleeve article and how many, with the catalogue entry and version it was picked from. Saved per order from the authoritative JSON catalogues (Q16). Implant continuing-education courses and institutes a client doctor trained with ("IE", "MI", "Chicago Maxicourse", "Pikos Institute"...), each with the treatment-planning guidelines that school teaches (e.g. "never use < 8 mm implants", "no cantilevers"); planners apply them to the doctor's cases. clinical.patient_identities

PHIAUDITV010 rls forced · tenant isolation audited traceable to legacy 19 columns
Protected identity of a patient: name, date of birth, sex and external identifiers, exactly one row per clinical.patients row (1:1, sharing its key). Split from the pseudonymous register so that every other table, screen and report works on patient_code alone (V3_DESIGN C3). This base table is NEVER granted to the application or read roles directly: they read it only through the SECURITY DEFINER functions clinical.fn_get_patient_identity / fn_list_patient_identities (V130), each call writing audit.phi_access_log; owner/admin hold the only direct access, and every change is audited by core.fn_audit_row with PHI values redacted. GDPR erasure anonymises the row in place. Date of birth is decoded from legacy Orders.patientBirthDate / OrderRep.DOB by the stage-40 decoder (Q2, U2: plain DATE behind access controls). Contains PHI.
columntypetags · constraintsmeaning
patient_idbigintpk on delete restrictThe pseudonymous patient this identity belongs to (clinical.patients.id); also the primary key, so a patient has at most one identity. · → clinical.patients
tenant_idbigintnot null on delete restrictOwning tenant; equals clinical.patients.tenant_id of patient_id (written together by the ETL and the patient-creation function). Row-level security scopes on it. · → core.tenants · default core.fn_current_tenant()
full_namecharacter varying(255)PHInot nullPatient name as entered by the client; migrated from Orders.dcmPatientName (the DICOM-style name string, often "Family^Given" or free text). Never printed outside PHI-cleared documents. [PHI]
given_namecharacter varying(120)PHIGiven (first) name when recorded separately; user input. NULL = not recorded separately (all migrated rows: legacy holds a single name string). [PHI]
family_namecharacter varying(120)PHIFamily (last) name when recorded separately; user input. NULL = not recorded separately (all migrated rows). [PHI]
date_of_birthdatePHICalendar date of birth (no time zone meaning); decoded from legacy Orders.patientBirthDate / OrderRep.DOB (XChaCha20-Poly1305 ciphertext, Unix seconds or date text, see dob_source_format) or entered by the client. Stored as plain DATE behind the access controls of this table (U2). NULL = no date of birth: see dob_status for whether the source had none ('absent') or had an undecodable/conflicting value ('quarantined'). [PHI]
sexcharacter varying(10)PHInot nullAdministrative sex as entered by the client: 'female'; 'male'; 'other' = recorded but neither; 'unknown' = not recorded (default; legacy has no reliable sex field). [PHI] · default 'unknown'::character varying
external_mrncharacter varying(120)PHIThe client practice's own medical record number for the patient, when the client supplies one; user input. NULL = not supplied. [PHI]
dicom_patient_idcharacter varying(120)PHIPatient ID found in the DICOM headers of the uploaded CBCT scan (tag 0010,0020), kept to match later scans to this patient; system-extracted. Moved here from v2 clinical.patients because it is a direct identifier. NULL = no scan header read yet. [PHI]
notestextPHIFree-text notes about the patient; user input. Moved here from v2 clinical.patients.notes because free text routinely names the patient. NULL = no notes. [PHI]
dob_source_formatcharacter varying(20)How the legacy date of birth was stored before decoding: 'xchacha20' = libsodium XChaCha20-Poly1305-IETF ciphertext Base64(nonce || ciphertext) of Unix-seconds text (Q2); 'unix_seconds' = plain Unix-seconds number from older paths; 'date_text' = a plain date string. Migration provenance for reconciliation; the key and raw value are never stored. NULL = no DOB in the source (dob_status 'absent'), the DOB was entered in threeddx3, or a quarantined value matched none of the three formats.
dob_statuscharacter varying(20)not nullOutcome of date-of-birth decoding: 'decoded' = date_of_birth holds a valid date (decoded from legacy, or entered in threeddx3); 'absent' = the source held no date of birth (default); 'quarantined' = the source held a value that failed decryption/parsing, was implausible, or conflicted between Orders and OrderRep - date_of_birth left NULL and the case listed in the stage-40 quarantine report (no PHI in logs) for manual resolution. · default 'absent'::character varying
legacy_idbigintID of the legacy row the date of birth was taken from (Orders.ID or OrderRep.ID, per legacy_source). NULL = identity created in threeddx3 or no DOB source row.
legacy_sourcecharacter varying(64)Legacy table the identity (in particular the DOB) came from: 'Orders' or 'OrderRep'. NULL = created in threeddx3.
legacy_keycharacter varying(200)Composite source key when one id is not enough. NULL = legacy_id identifies the source row.

constraints (10)
namekinddefinitionrule
pk_patient_identitiesPRIMARY KEYPRIMARY KEY (patient_id)A patient has at most one identity row (1:1 with clinical.patients).
fk_patient_identities__patient_idFOREIGN KEYFOREIGN KEY (patient_id) REFERENCES clinical.patients(id) ON DELETE RESTRICTAn identity belongs to an existing patient. RESTRICT, not CASCADE: a patient row must never take its PHI away silently; erasure anonymises the identity explicitly (with a legal-hold check) and the patient row is only soft-deleted.
fk_patient_identities__tenant_idFOREIGN KEYFOREIGN KEY (tenant_id) REFERENCES core.tenants(id) ON DELETE RESTRICTEvery row belongs to exactly one tenant (data owner). RESTRICT: a tenant with data cannot be deleted; tenants are retired by state, never removed.
ck_patient_identities__absent_has_no_formatCHECKCHECK ((((dob_status)::text <> 'absent'::text) OR (dob_source_format IS NULL)))If the source held no date of birth there is no source format to record.
ck_patient_identities__dob_rangeCHECKCHECK ((date_of_birth >= '1900-01-01'::date))A date of birth before 1900-01-01 is a decoding error (Unix-seconds or epoch defaults decode to 1970 and are caught by the ETL plausibility check instead); future dates are rejected by the ETL and the application because a CHECK cannot use the current date.
ck_patient_identities__dob_source_formatCHECKCHECK (((dob_source_format)::text = ANY ((ARRAY['xchacha20'::character varying, 'unix_seconds'::character varying, 'date_text'::character varying])::text[])))Legacy DOB format is one of the three formats found in Orders.patientBirthDate / OrderRep.DOB (Q2): xchacha20, unix_seconds, date_text.
ck_patient_identities__dob_statusCHECKCHECK (((dob_status)::text = ANY ((ARRAY['decoded'::character varying, 'absent'::character varying, 'quarantined'::character varying])::text[])))DOB decoding outcome is one of decoded, absent, quarantined.
ck_patient_identities__dob_status_consistentCHECKCHECK (((((dob_status)::text = 'decoded'::text) AND (date_of_birth IS NOT NULL)) OR (((dob_status)::text = ANY ((ARRAY['absent'::character varying, 'quarantined'::character varying])::text[])) AND (date_of_birth IS NULL))))A date of birth is present exactly when the status is decoded; absent and quarantined rows carry no date, so a failed decode can never leave a wrong date behind.
ck_patient_identities__full_name_not_blankCHECKCHECK ((btrim((full_name)::text) <> ''::text))A patient identity always carries a non-blank name; orders without a patient name create no patient.
ck_patient_identities__sexCHECKCHECK (((sex)::text = ANY ((ARRAY['female'::character varying, 'male'::character varying, 'other'::character varying, 'unknown'::character varying])::text[])))Sex is one of female, male, other, unknown.

clinical.patients

AUDITV010 rls forced · tenant isolation traceable to legacy 13 columns
Pseudonymous patient register: one row per patient of one client (dental practice), identified only by a system-generated patient_code and uuid. Holds no name, date of birth or other identity - those are in clinical.patient_identities (1:1), which is PHI and reachable only through logged functions (V3_DESIGN C3, HIPAA minimum necessary, GDPR pseudonymisation). Referenced by orders.orders, orders.cases and clinical.tooth_charts. Legacy has no patient table: rows are derived from Orders.dcmPatientName de-duplicated per (client, name); legacy_source = 'Orders' and legacy_id = Orders.ID of the first order that created the patient (v2 left all 464,897 patients without a source mapping - review finding). Soft-deleted via deleted_at; erasure anonymises the identity row instead of deleting this one.

Unique per tenant. TO CONFIRM: whether the business wants a sequential format from core.number_sequences instead. · default ('PT-'::text || upper(substr(replace((gen_random_uuid())::text, '-'::text, ''::text), 1, 16)))

clinical.sleeve_manufacturer_articles

AUDITSNAPSHOTV010 rls forced · tenant isolation traceable to legacy 15 columns
The sleeve / fixation-pin article catalogue as offered per manufacturer: one row per (manufacturer, part id) entry of ThreeDDXSleevesArticleNumbers.json, twin of legacy sleeveArticleNumbers (UNIQUE(partID, manufacturerID), ~385 rows). clinical.surgical_kit_protocol_rows

AUDITV010 rls forced · tenant isolation traceable to legacy 19 columns
Queryable projection of a surgical kit protocol version: one row per (implant line, diameter, length) combination in the document (about 690 rows over the 22 kit files), so planners and reports can ask "which kits support a 4.1 x 10 implant" without parsing JSON. The drilling steps stay in JSONB (steps) because the 22 kit files use 22 different step vocabularies (tissuePunch / initialDrill / vDrill[] / masterTube[] / KeySeq ...); normalising them into step rows needs a canonical drill-step taxonomy from a clinical owner that does not exist yet (digest 01 ambiguity 5). Child of surgical_kit_protocols: rows of an approved version must not change (enforced with the parent's state by a V110 trigger), and are deleted only with a draft parent.

clinical.surgical_kit_protocols

AUDITV010 rls forced · tenant isolation audited traceable to legacy 24 columns
Versioned drilling protocol of a surgical kit (regulated record, 21 CFR Part 820 / Part 11): one row per version of one kit definition - for each implant line, diameter and length, the tissue punch, drill sequence and colour codes, drill stops, driver, sleeve position and kit notes that the SG instruction sheet prints. Loaded from the 20 SGInstuctions/Kits/Data/*.json files (format legacy_kit_v1) and 2 statics/DrillingKits/*.json files (form_v2); the full original JSON stays in document and drives the renderer, with a queryable projection in surgical_kit_protocol_rows. Lifecycle draft -> in_review -> approved -> superseded; an approved or superseded version is immutable (trg_surgical_kit_protocols__immutable_when_approved) and a correction inserts version_no + 1 with supersedes_id; at most one approved version per protocol_code. Electronic signatures reference (id, version_no, content_hash) in compliance.electronic_signatures. Migrated versions load as draft because protocol approval ownership is pending (Q15).

TO CONFIRM. · → clinical.surgical_kits

clinical.surgical_kits

AUDITV010 rls forced · tenant isolation traceable to legacy 16 columns
Guided-surgery drilling kits the lab designs guides for (Nobel, Straumann, Astra EV, BioHorizons, the "Pilot 1.1-2.5 mm" pseudo-kits, "Other", "Universal"...): one row per kit in the SGKits.json pick-list (114 entries) plus Relu surgicalKits. clinical.tooth_charts

PHI-RISKAUDITV010 rls forced · tenant isolation traceable to legacy 17 columns
The dental chart submitted with an order: which arch is treated and, through tooth_sites, which teeth are missing, to be extracted, implanted, crowned, etc. One row per chart of an order (or of one order item when the item has its own chart). Migrated from the five comma-separated teeth columns of legacy Orders (TeethMissed, TeethExtract, ImplantsSites, abutmentSites, crownSites) plus archOfInterest; one chart per order that recorded any teeth. Tooth numbers are always stored in FDI (U11); the notation the client charted in is kept in source_notation. Clinical record: not soft-deleted; changes are audited.

Views

clinical.v_patients_masked

view 9 columns
Minimum-necessary view of patients for read and reporting roles: patient code, owning client, initials, birth year, sex and DOB decode status — never the full name, full date of birth, MRN or DICOM id. Filters to the session tenant explicitly (definer view). Full identity is available only through clinical.fn_get_patient_identity, which logs the access.
columntypemeaning
patient_idbigint
tenant_idbigint
patient_codecharacter varying(40)
contact_idbigint
initialstext
birth_yearinteger
sexcharacter varying(10)
dob_statuscharacter varying(20)
created_attimestamp with time zone
definition
 SELECT p.id AS patient_id,
    p.tenant_id,
    p.patient_code,
    p.contact_id,
    upper("left"(btrim(pi.given_name::text), 1)) || upper("left"(btrim(pi.family_name::text), 1)) AS initials,
    EXTRACT(year FROM pi.date_of_birth)::integer AS birth_year,
    pi.sex,
    pi.dob_status,
    p.created_at
   FROM clinical.patients p
     LEFT JOIN clinical.patient_identities pi ON pi.patient_id = p.id
  WHERE p.tenant_id = core.fn_current_tenant() AND p.deleted_at IS NULL;

fn_fdi_to_universal(p_fdi core.fdi_tooth)smallint
app_rw, owner, read
Converts an FDI permanent tooth number (11-48) to the American Universal (ADA) number 1-32 for display to clients who chart in Universal notation; exact inverse of clinical.fn_universal_to_fdi. Pure and immutable. Raises invalid_parameter_value for deciduous teeth (51-85), which have letters, not numbers, in Universal notation. Returns NULL for NULL input.
fn_get_patient_identity(p_patient_id bigint, p_purpose text)SETOF clinical.patient_identitiessecurity definer
app_rw, owner
HIPAA minimum-necessary gateway to one patient's identity (name, DOB, sex, MRN, DICOM id). Requires a tenant and a stated purpose; returns only the current tenant's patient; every successful call writes audit.phi_access_log (who, role, patient, purpose, request). The base table is never granted to app or read roles.
fn_list_patient_identities(p_patient_ids bigint[], p_purpose text)SETOF clinical.patient_identitiessecurity definer
app_rw, owner
Bulk form of fn_get_patient_identity for list screens: up to 500 patients per call, current tenant only, purpose required, one audit.phi_access_log row per patient returned.
fn_reject_identity_edit_when_invoiced()triggertrigger
app_rw, owner
BEFORE UPDATE on clinical.patient_identities: the patient name and date of birth printed on an issued invoice cannot be changed afterwards (they would silently rewrite a financial document). The migrator may bypass for approved rectifications (GDPR Art. 16) with app.bypass_financial_lock.
fn_universal_to_fdi(p_universal smallint)core.fdi_tooth
app_rw, owner, read
Converts an American Universal (ADA) permanent tooth number 1-32 to FDI two-digit notation (1 = 18 upper right third molar, 8 = 11, 9 = 21, 16 = 28, 17 = 38, 24 = 31, 25 = 41, 32 = 48). Pure and immutable: used by the API edge and the ETL so every stored tooth number (core.fdi_tooth) is FDI regardless of the client's numbering preference (crm.contacts.numbering_system, U11). Raises invalid_parameter_value for anything outside 1-32; deciduous Universal letters A-T are not handled. Returns NULL for NULL input.

vouchers

9 tables · 156 columns · 2 functions

Prepaid credit: voucher types, vouchers, scope and coverage, promo codes and redemptions, and the balance ledger.

Prepaid credit. Balances on vouchers.vouchers are derived from the ledger vouchers.voucher_transactions by trigger — never write a balance. Migrated ledger rows are reconstructed by a port of the CP's voucher_fill and carry reconstruction_method; main, Engel and service-voucher streams stay separate (scope).

vouchers.voucher_transactions

FINANCIALAUDITSNAPSHOTV012 rls forced · tenant isolation append-only traceable to legacy 25 columns
The voucher ledger: one row per movement of credit on one voucher (issue, redeem, refund, adjust, expire, reinstate, transfer). Single ledger replacing legacy voucher_transaction (main stream), EngelVoucherTransactions (engel stream) and ServiceVouchers (service stream); the three streams are told apart by scope and never mixed. Historical main-stream rows are reconstructed by the PostgreSQL port of newcp/scripts/voucher_fill.php (Q19) with a deterministic source key, so a rerun produces the same rows. Balances on vouchers.vouchers are derived from it by the V100 insert trigger. Append-only: corrections are new adjust rows (trg_voucher_transactions__append_only). Financial record.
columntypetags · constraintsmeaning
idbigintpkSurrogate key of the movement; system-generated. Not the business order of movements (see sequence_no).
tenant_idbigintnot null on delete restrictOwning tenant (core.tenants); filtered by RLS. · → core.tenants · default core.fn_current_tenant()
voucher_idbigintnot null on delete restrictVoucher whose balance moves (vouchers.vouchers). Legacy voucher_transaction.voucher_id holds the voucher ORDER id (Orders.ID, sometimes prefixed '0_'), resolved via Orders.VrID -> OrderVoucher.ID (v2 defect 37). · → vouchers.vouchers
scopecharacter varying(20)not nullLedger stream the movement belongs to; streams are never mixed in one balance computation: 'main' = OrderVoucher prepaid/general credit (legacy voucher_transaction, reconstructed by voucher_fill.php); 'engel' = Engel programme case vouchers (legacy EngelVoucherTransactions); 'service' = per-sub-order service voucher deductions (legacy ServiceVouchers). TO CONFIRM: that a voucher only ever carries movements of one scope (to be enforced by V100 once confirmed). · default 'main'::character varying
sequence_nointegernot nullPosition of the movement within its voucher, 1, 2, 3 ...: the deterministic order in which balance_after is computed. For reconstructed rows assigned by effective_at, then the source key, so equal timestamps still order the same way on every run (voucher_fill.php instead added (n+1)*100 seconds to the time). Unique per voucher; > 0.
txn_kindvouchers.txn_kindnot nullKind of movement (vouchers.txn_kind): 'issue' = credit granted (voucher_fill opening row at dateSent); 'redeem' = credit consumed by an order item; 'refund' = consumed credit returned to the voucher; 'adjust' = reconciliation correction (voucher_fill 'refund by: SYSTEM' extra-credit row is a positive adjust, 'deduction by: SYSTEM' missing-amount row a negative adjust; manual deductions/refunds from the edit-voucher page); 'expire' = unused credit lapsed; 'reinstate' = lapsed credit restored; 'transfer' = credit moved to another voucher.
order_idbiginton delete restrictOrder the movement concerns (orders.orders): the consuming order for a redeem, the voucher sale order for an issue (voucher_fill writes the voucher order id). NULL = movement not tied to an order (expiry, system adjustment, manual correction). · → orders.orders
order_item_idbiginton delete restrictOrder item the movement concerns as recorded by the source (v2 column; for an issue row the voucher sale line). Requires order_id. NULL = no item recorded. · → orders.order_items
consuming_order_item_idbiginton delete restrictService (order item) whose credit use this movement records: the sub-order whose voucherIds allocation string named this voucher in voucher_fill.php (Conversion, TP, SG, Report, restoration via ServiceVouchersView, iSmile sub-order). Provenance required by the review (F04). Never set on an issue row. NULL = movement not caused by a service (issue, expiry, system adjustment) or the consuming service could not be resolved. · → orders.order_items
sellable_item_idbiginton delete restrictCatalogue service the credit was spent on (catalog.sellable_items). NULL = not a service consumption or service not resolved. · → catalog.sellable_items
credit_deltacore.money_amountFINANCIALnot nullSigned change of the voucher's money balance, in currency_code: positive raises it (issue, refund, reinstate, positive adjust), negative lowers it (redeem, expire, negative adjust); 0 for pure case movements. [FINANCIAL]
case_deltaintegernot nullSigned change of the case balance on a case-count (Engel) voucher; 0 for money movements. · default 0
balance_aftercore.money_amountFINANCIALnot nullRemaining money credit of the voucher after this movement, in currency_code, in sequence_no order (legacy voucher_remaining / EngelVoucherTransactions.RemainingInVoucher); never negative. Lets reconciliation scan rather than sum recursively. [FINANCIAL]
currency_codecore.currency_codeon delete restrictCurrency of credit_delta and balance_after. NULL = the voucher's currency_code (the normal case; a value is stored only if it must be stated explicitly, and then must equal the voucher's). · → core.currencies
reasoncharacter varying(255)Short reason for the movement, e.g. 'refund by: SYSTEM', 'deduction by: SYSTEM', 'service voucher deduction', or a staff explanation for a manual correction. NULL = no reason recorded (ordinary redemption).
source_allocationcharacter varying(500)SNAPSHOTThe legacy allocation string the movement was derived from, copied verbatim: the sub-order's voucherIds list '<voucherOrderId>:<amount>,...' (voucher_transaction.new_voucher_ids_record). Kept so a reconstructed amount can be re-checked against its evidence. NULL = not derived from an allocation string. [SNAPSHOT]
legacy_cases_creditintegerMigrated verbatim from voucher_transaction.casesCredit / EngelVoucherTransactions.casesCredit. TO CONFIRM (Q17): believed to be the case balance after the movement, not a delta, so it is not used as case_delta until confirmed. NULL = not an Engel movement.
reconstruction_methodcharacter varying(30)not nullHow the row came to exist: 'recorded' = written when the movement happened (live threeddx3 rows, and legacy rows copied as stored, e.g. manual deductions/refunds and EngelVoucherTransactions); 'voucher_fill_v1' = reconstructed by version 1 of the PostgreSQL port of voucher_fill.php fillVoucherRows() from consuming-service evidence (Q19), including its opening, extra-credit and missing-amount rows; 'opening_balance' = one synthetic row setting the balance where no movement history can be reconstructed. A new reconstruction algorithm gets a new value (voucher_fill_v2), never a silent change. · default 'recorded'::character varying
actor_kindcore.actor_kindnot nullWho caused the movement (core.actor_kind): 'user' = a staff or portal user; 'system' = a job, trigger or the migration; 'integration' = an external system; 'anonymous' = unauthenticated request. · default 'user'::core.actor_kind
actor_user_idbigintUser who caused the movement. No FK by design: the ledger is append-only (an ON DELETE SET NULL would be an UPDATE the append-only trigger rejects) and must survive user deletion. NULL = not a user action (system, migration, integration).
effective_attimestamp with time zonenot nullUTC instant the movement takes effect in business terms: for a redemption the consuming service's latest end/sent/billed/update time, never earlier than the voucher's creation (voucher_fill.php GREATEST(voucher dateSent, timeEnd, timeSent, timeUpdate), without its +100 s de-duplication offsets); for the opening row the voucher's dateSent (+5 s / +10 s for the system extra/missing rows as in the script); otherwise the time of the event. Legacy times are America/New_York and converted to UTC.
occurred_attimestamp with time zoneAUDITnot nullUTC instant the movement was recorded in the system: now() for live rows; the stored legacy transaction_time / TransactionTime / deductedTime for copied legacy rows; the load time for reconstructed rows. [AUDIT] · default now()
legacy_idbigintSource row id where the source has one (EngelVoucherTransactions.id, ServiceVouchers.id). NULL = source has no row id (voucher_transaction, reconstructed rows: see legacy_key) or created in threeddx3.
legacy_sourcecharacter varying(64)Source of the row: 'voucher_transaction', 'EngelVoucherTransactions', 'ServiceVouchers' or 'voucher_fill_v1'. NULL = created in threeddx3.
legacy_keycharacter varying(200)Stable deterministic composite source key (legacy voucher_transaction has no row id): for copied voucher_transaction rows its primary key '<voucher_id>|<transaction_time>|<order_id>'; for voucher_fill_v1 rows '<voucher order id>|<row role: open, extra, missing, use>|<order_type_id>|<sub_order_id>|<serviceID>|<occurrence>'. Same input data always yields the same key, so a rerun cannot load a row twice. Required for every non-recorded row. NULL = live row or a source with legacy_id.

vouchers.vouchers

PHI-RISKPIIFINANCIALAUDITV012 rls forced · tenant isolation audited traceable to legacy 37 columns
One prepaid credit granted to a client: a sold prepaid package (legacy OrderVoucher), a GFMR programme voucher (GFMRVoucher), an Engel case voucher (EngelVoucher) or a promotional voucher. Holds the balance columns, which are derived from the ledger vouchers.voucher_transactions by V100 trigger and never written directly by the application; the CHECKs make an overdrawn or inconsistent balance impossible (v2 defect 36). Owned by the vouchers module; status-driven lifecycle, no soft delete (cancel instead); financial, so FKs to it are RESTRICT. Contains PII only through the linked client.

Functions

functionreturnsexecute granted tobehaviour
fn_apply_transaction()triggertrigger
app_rw, owner
BEFORE INSERT on vouchers.voucher_transactions — the only writer of voucher balances. Rejects any movement that would take the balance below zero; for movements created in threeddx3 (no legacy key) also rejects redeeming an expired, suspended or cancelled voucher, or one that belongs to a different client than the order. Sets balance_after and moves exactly one balance column per kind: issue/adjust(+) -> issued; redeem/adjust(-) -> consumed; refund -> consumed decreases (credit returned to the voucher, as legacy voucher_fill 'refund by: SYSTEM'); expire/reinstate -> expired; transfer -> refunded (credit leaving the voucher). Case counters follow issue/redeem/refund/expire.
fn_draw_down_order(p_contact_id bigint, p_order_id bigint, p_type_codes text[], p_on date)TABLE(voucher_id bigint, priority integer, remaining core.money_amount)
app_rw, owner
Candidate vouchers to pay an order line, in the order the business consumes them: a voucher linked to this order first, then general credit, then by-case vouchers, then oldest first. Excludes vouchers linked to a different order, expired, exhausted, suspended or cancelled ones. Engel priority (GFMR, then Engel, then General, then Normal — owner Q17 documentation) is applied by the caller through p_type_codes ordering.

Types and domains

typedefinitionmeaning
vouchers.txn_kindenum: issue, redeem, refund, adjust, expire, reinstate, transferVoucher ledger movement: 'issue' = credit granted; 'redeem' = credit consumed by an order item; 'refund' = consumed credit returned; 'adjust' = reconciliation correction (e.g. voucher_fill adjustment rows); 'expire' = unused credit lapsed; 'reinstate' = lapsed credit restored; 'transfer' = moved to another voucher.

workflow

13 tables · 196 columns · 2 functions

One workflow engine: definitions per service family, states, transitions, instances, history, legacy status decoding, tasks and their history.

One state machine. v3 has a workflow definition per service family and legacy service dimension, and workflow.legacy_status_codes decodes every legacy status id to a state. Tasks record every due-date change with a reason.

workflow.legacy_status_codes

AUDITSNAPSHOTV013 rls forced · tenant isolation traceable to legacy 12 columns
Translation of a legacy numeric status code into a state, per definition: the same legacy code means different things on different product lines (GFMR and Other both reuse 138/145; ordersStatus.json reuses 1-11 and 21-24 across families), so the key is (definition, legacy status id). Seeded by the ETL from OrdersFlow and ec2 statics/ordersStatus.json (97 statuses in 15 families); used to load item status history and to answer legacy-code questions. Configuration; goes with its definition.
