workflow.workflow_definitions

AUDITV013 rls forced · tenant isolation traceable to legacy 19 columns
A state machine: the ordered set of states and allowed transitions that one kind of entity (usually an order item of one service family) moves through. Legacy OrdersFlow keyed its flows on (OrderType, isDigital, serviceID) — 18 distinct combinations; v3 keeps one definition per combination (review F05; v2 ignored serviceID and collapsed them to 16). Versioned by (code, version); a definition in use is deactivated, not deleted. Seeded by ETL stage 60 / V2nn seeds.

workflow.workflow_history

PHI-RISKAUDITV013 rls forced · tenant isolation append-only traceable to legacy 15 columns
Every state change of a workflow instance: from, to, which transition, who (user and the role they acted in), when, and how long the instance spent in the previous state. Written by the V100 transition trigger, so history can never diverge from the current state; migrated from legacy status history tables. Append-only (trg_workflow_history__append_only); corrections are new rows. Large (millions of rows).

workflow.workflow_instances

AUDITV013 rls forced · tenant isolation 16 columns
One run of a workflow definition for one entity (usually an order item) on one track: where it is now, when it started and finished, and its SLA due time. An item may run several tracks at once (Final AoX: Try-In, Ti Bar and Zirconia in parallel). Each open legacy item gets the definition of its own (order type, isDigital, serviceID) and its mapped current state (review F05), not the first definition. State changes are validated by the V100 trigger, which writes workflow_history.

fn_require_due_date_reason()triggertrigger

BEFORE UPDATE OF due_at on workflow.tasks: a due date may change only when a workflow.task_due_date_changes row (with its reason) for the same task and new date was written in the same transaction (changed_at = transaction time). original_due_at, once set, never changes. Legacy evidence: ReasonsForChangeDueDateCSTasks, Tasks/updateDueDate.

app_rw, owner
BEFORE UPDATE on workflow.workflow_instances: rejects a state change that no workflow_transitions row allows for that definition (from the old state, or from any state when from_state_id is NULL), then writes the workflow_history row with the acting user and role and the time spent in the previous state — so history can never diverge from state. The migrator may set app.bypass_workflow to replay legacy histories that broke the rules.

Internal notes between departments, attached to an order or one order item. Recipients are rows, not a semicolon-separated string.

collaboration.internal_history

PHIPHI-RISKAUDITV014 rls forced · tenant isolation traceable to legacy 19 columns
An internal note about an order or one of its services, written by staff for other departments (legacy OrdersInternalHistory): either a plain note or an action request that a team later marks as acted on. Not visible to the client. order_item_id distinguishes an order-level note from a note about one service; recipients and attachments are child tables; a task may be raised from a note. History: kept for the life of the order (RESTRICT). Contains PHI (free text names patients).

production.production_jobs

PHI-RISKAUDITV015 rls forced · tenant isolation traceable to legacy 26 columns
One unit of production work on an order item: a design, a print, a manufacturing, assembly or finishing step, or a rework. One row per (order item, kind of work, attempt); a remake or re-run is a new row with a higher attempt_number. Owned by the production module; parent of job_assignments, print_runs and quality.inspections. Legacy had no job entity (production state lived as columns on SubOrderServices/OrderSG); the ETL derives one job per item that reached production. Not soft-deleted: a job that will not be done is status 'cancelled'. The approval gate (no production before the design approval passed) is enforced in V100.

production.reports

AUDITV015 rls forced · tenant isolation audited traceable to legacy 24 columns
A production report (header): guide design, restoration, mold, daily treatment-plan, printer build, night build, shipment, magnet count and closers reports, each for one date and optionally one work centre; production.report_lines holds the orders/items it covers. Production reports are regulated records (FDA 21 CFR 820 device history record, Part 11 electronic records; V3_DESIGN.md C6): each row is one VERSION of a report. A version moves draft -> in_review -> approved; once approved it is immutable (trg_reports__immutable_when_approved) and the only allowed change is approved -> superseded when a correcting version is inserted with supersedes_id pointing to it. Electronic signatures (compliance.electronic_signatures) reference the exact (id, version_no, content_hash). Migrated from GuideDesignReports, RestorationReports, restorationServiceReports, MoldsReports, DailyTPReports and PrinterReports; migrated reports were final in legacy and load as approved without a hash or approver (legacy kept none). Approved and superseded versions are never deleted.
columntypetags · constraintsmeaning
idbigintpkSurrogate key of this report version; system-generated.
uuiduuidunique not nullPublic identifier of this report version for the API and signature links; system-generated. · default gen_random_uuid()
tenant_idbigintnot null on delete restrictTenant that owns the report (core.tenants; FK added in V090). · → core.tenants · default core.fn_current_tenant()
report_kindcharacter varying(40)not nullWhich production report: 'guide_design' = daily surgical-guide design report (GuideDesignReports); 'restoration' = restoration report (RestorationReports, restorationServiceReports); 'mold' = molds report (MoldsReports); 'daily_tp' = daily treatment-plan report (DailyTPReports); 'printer_build' = printer build report (PrinterReports); 'night_build' = overnight build report; 'shipment' = shipping-day report; 'magnet_count' = magnet stock count; 'closers' = end-of-day closers report (Boston daily reports).
work_center_idbiginton delete restrictWork centre the report covers (production.work_centers). NULL = tenant-wide report or not recorded (migrated reports). · → production.work_centers

approved_by_user_idbiginton delete restrictStaff user who approved this version (iam.users; FK in V090, RESTRICT). Required for an approved version created in threeddx3. NULL = not approved yet, or a migrated report whose approver legacy did not keep. · → iam.users
approved_attimestamp with time zoneUTC instant this version was approved. NULL = not approved yet, or a migrated report (legacy kept no approval time).
statuscharacter varying(20)not nullv2 business status, kept because the ETL and existing screens write it: 'draft' = being prepared; 'submitted' = sent for review; 'approved' = final; 'void' = withdrawn before approval. It must agree with state: status 'approved' if and only if state is approved or superseded. New code should drive state; status follows it. · default 'draft'::character varying
version_nosmallintnot nullVersion number of the report, 1 for the first version, previous + 1 for each correcting version (the successor rule is enforced in V100). · default 1
statecharacter varying(20)not nullRegulated-record version state: 'draft' = editable; 'in_review' = submitted for approval, still editable by the reviewer; 'approved' = released and immutable (21 CFR Part 11); 'superseded' = an approved version replaced by a newer approved correction, kept unchanged for history. 'migrated' = loaded from the legacy system, where no Part 11 approval existed; immutable like an approved version but makes no approval claim (approved_by/at stay NULL). · default 'draft'::character varying
supersedes_idbiginton delete restrictPrevious version this version corrects (production.reports). NULL = first version of the report. · → production.reports
content_hashcore.sha256_hexSHA-256 of the canonical content of this version (header plus its lines) computed at approval; electronic signatures store the same hash so any later change is detectable. NULL = not approved yet, or a migrated report (TO CONFIRM whether the ETL should hash migrated reports).
superseded_attimestamp with time zoneUTC instant this version was superseded by a correction. NULL = not superseded (current or never approved).
summaryjsonbnot nullReport totals and header figures as captured on the report form (counts per category). Part of the signed content; never filtered on. · default '{}'::jsonb
legacy_idbigintSource row id when migrated (the legacy report table's own id). NULL = created in threeddx3. Its presence exempts a migrated approved report from the approver/hash requirement.
legacy_sourcecharacter varying(64)Legacy table the row came from (GuideDesignReports, RestorationReports, restorationServiceReports, MoldsReports, DailyTPReports, PrinterReports). NULL = created in threeddx3.
legacy_keycharacter varying(200)Composite legacy key when one id is not enough. NULL = not needed.

updated_attimestamp with time zoneAUDITnot nullUTC instant of the last change; maintained by trg_reports__touch_updated_at (frozen once approved). [AUDIT] · default now()
created_by_user_idbigintAUDITiam.users.id of the person who created the row; no FK by design (actor history must survive user deletion). NULL = system or migration. [AUDIT]
updated_by_user_idbigintAUDITiam.users.id of the person who last changed the row; no FK by design. NULL = never changed by a person. [AUDIT]

quality.form_templates

AUDITV016 rls forced · tenant isolation traceable to legacy 20 columns
One version of a QC (quality control) checklist form, e.g. the Night Guard Restoration QC checklist, controlled document WI-21-01 Rev E (owner answer Q8). One row per (tenant, code, version); sections and items hang below it. Exactly one version per code is 'active' at a time (uq_form_templates__tenant_id__code__active) - the legacy getActiveQCForm behaviour. A change to the checklist is a new version row; the old version is set 'deprecated'/'archived' and stays so that past inspections still resolve to the exact items they answered. Owned by the quality module. Fewer than ~100 rows, so the catalog FKs are deliberately not indexed.

quality.inspections

PHI-RISKAUDITV016 rls forced · tenant isolation audited traceable to legacy 27 columns
One QC inspection of an order, order item or production job against one QC template version, with its outcome and score (legacy QCFormOrderEvaluation; round 2 is the second-guide QC). QC records are regulated records (21 CFR 820 acceptance activities, Part 11 electronic records; V3_DESIGN.md C6): each row is one VERSION of an inspection record. A version moves draft -> in_review -> approved; once approved it is immutable (trg_inspections__immutable_when_approved) and a correction is a new row with supersedes_id pointing to it, after which the old version may only move to 'superseded'. Electronic signatures (compliance.electronic_signatures) reference the exact (id, version_no, content_hash). Parent of inspection_results; nonconformities link to failed inspections. Never deleted once approved; RESTRICT from orders, items and jobs.

quality.nonconformities

PHI-RISKAUDITV016 rls forced · tenant isolation traceable to legacy 22 columns
A recorded nonconformity (QMS, 21 CFR 820 nonconforming product): something produced or found that does not meet its requirement, with severity, investigation, root cause and corrective action, usually raised from a failed inspection and resolved through a workflow task. One row per nonconformity. Owned by the quality module; escalation to complaints/CAPA lives in compliance. Quality history: never deleted (closed with status 'closed'), RESTRICT from inspections and order items.

inventory

8 tables · 138 columns · 1 functions

Stock: warehouses, locations, items, stock levels and movements, serialised units, loaner-kit rentals, reservations.

Physical goods: stock levels derived from movements by trigger, serialised units with warranty, loaner-kit rentals, and reservations that cannot overlap for the same unit (EXCLUDE constraint).

inventory.items

AUDITV017 rls forced · tenant isolation traceable to legacy 20 columns
A stock-keeping item 3DDX holds: consumables (resin, sleeves, pins), assets (printers for sale or internal use), kits (loaner surgical kits, one item per kit type), components and packaging. One row per item; individual physical units of serialised items are inventory.serialised_units. Owned by the inventory module; links to the catalog article/sellable item it fulfils. Migrated from LoanerKit types (one item per distinct LoanerKit.Type). Master data: deactivated with is_active.

inventory.reservations

AUDITV017 rls forced · tenant isolation traceable to legacy 17 columns
A hold on stock for an order item: a quantity of a non-serialised item, or one specific serialised unit (a loaner kit, a printer) for a period [reserved_from, held_until). One row per hold. A serialised unit cannot be held by two open reservations whose periods overlap (ex_reservations__unit_no_overlap). Feeds inventory.stock_levels.quantity_reserved (V110). Transient operational data: released/consumed/expired rows are kept for history; deleted with the order item it holds stock for.

inventory.stock_levels

AUDITV017 rls forced · tenant isolation 10 columns
Current stock balance of one item in one warehouse (and optionally one location): on hand, reserved, available. A materialised balance derived from inventory.stock_movements and inventory.reservations and maintained by trigger (V110); never edited by hand, rebuildable from the ledger. One row per (item, warehouse, location). Derived data: deleted with its item or warehouse (CASCADE), carries no history of its own.

inventory.stock_movements

AUDITV017 rls forced · tenant isolation append-only traceable to legacy 20 columns
Append-only stock ledger: one row per movement of an item (receipt, issue, return, adjustment, transfer, write-off) with quantity, warehouses and the order/shipment that caused it. inventory.stock_levels is the balance derived from it (V110 trigger). Corrections are new movements (an adjustment), never edits: UPDATE and DELETE are rejected by trg_stock_movements__append_only, so every link is RESTRICT. No legacy source today (legacy kept no stock ledger).

Functions

functionreturnsexecute granted tobehaviour
fn_apply_movement()triggertrigger
app_rw, owner
AFTER INSERT on inventory.stock_movements (append-only): applies the movement to inventory.stock_levels — receipts and returns add, issues and write-offs subtract, adjustments carry their own sign, transfers move between warehouses. Stock may not go negative (ck_stock_levels__quantities_non_negative rejects the movement).

archive.packages

PHI-RISKAUDITV018 rls forced · tenant isolation traceable to legacy 23 columns
One physical package received for an order and kept in the Boston case archive (impressions, models, bites, guides), from scanning its tracking barcode at intake through storage to shipping back or disposal. One row per package; contents in archive.package_items. Owned by the archive module (ServiceAPI ArchivedPackages, CP mobile). Migrated from legacy ArchivedPackages (~18.5k rows). Timestamps are UTC instants: legacy CreationDate/UpdatedDate were stored shifted by a fixed -5 h by the legacy triggers and were corrected by +5 h on migration (owner answer Q1). Status changes follow expected -> received -> stored -> retrieved | shipped_back | disposed (transition trigger in V110). Never deleted; disposal is a status.

NULL = not recorded. Migrated from ArchivedPackages.archOfInterest (legacy column comment: 0 maxilla, 1 mandible, 2 both - see schema notes on the ETL mapping).

shipping.couriers

AUDITV019 rls forced · tenant isolation traceable to legacy 15 columns
A carrier or delivery channel 3DDX ships with: UPS, FedEx, DHL, USPS, and the pseudo-courier 'Digital delivery'. One row per carrier per tenant. Legacy stored the carrier as an integer code (OrderShipmentDetails.serviceProvider: 0 UPS, 1 FedEx, 2 DHL, 3 USPS, -1 = delivered digitally); each code is a row here with legacy_id = that code, and -1 is the row with delivery_mode = 'digital' (seeded in V2nn), so "digitally delivered" is a real value, not an error. Master data: deactivated with is_active. A handful of rows, so the integration_provider_id FK is deliberately not indexed.

shipping.labels

PIIAUDITV019 rls forced · tenant isolation audited 13 columns
A carrier label issued for a shipment, with its file and tracking number. shipping.shipments

PHI-RISKPIIFINANCIALAUDITSNAPSHOTV019 rls forced · tenant isolation audited traceable to legacy 40 columns
One consignment between 3DDX and a client (or digital delivery of an order's output): outbound guides, models and restorations, inbound impressions for the archive, returning loaner kits. One row per consignment with its courier, tracking number, status and costs; contents in shipment_items, labels in labels, carrier scans in tracking_events. The destination address is copied onto the row at shipping time (ship_to_* columns, [SNAPSHOT] [PII]) so the record shows where the parcel actually went even after the client edits or deprecates the address book entry. Migrated from legacy OrderShipmentDetails (~19.5k rows). Shipping history: never deleted (cancelled is a status); RESTRICT from orders and clients. Contains PII.

PIIAUDITV019 rls forced · tenant isolation append-only 9 columns
Append-only log of carrier tracking scans for a shipment (picked up, in transit, out for delivery, delivered, exception), from courier webhooks or polling. billing.charges

PHI-RISKFINANCIALAUDITV020 rls forced · tenant isolation append-only traceable to legacy 20 columns
Append-only charge ledger: one row per chargeable event (an order item charged, a shipping or rush fee, a manual adjustment) or per reversal of one. Answers "what were total charges yesterday?" without touching orders; the net charge of an order item is SUM(amount) over its rows. A row's existence is the charged state (there is no status column). Uncharge (CP restOrder/uncharge, voucher/uncharge, unchargeIsmileSubOrder; D4 rule 6) inserts a reversing row with charge_kind credit/refund, a negative amount and reverses_charge_id pointing at the original; rows are never updated or deleted (trg_charges__append_only). Owned by the billing module. [FINANCIAL]
columntypetags · constraintsmeaning

contact_idbigintnot null on delete restrictClient charged (crm.contacts). For a reversal it is the same client as the original charge. · → crm.contacts
order_idbiginton delete restrictOrder the charge belongs to (orders.orders). NULL = a charge not tied to an order (annual fee, account-level adjustment). · → orders.orders
order_item_idbiginton delete restrictOrder item charged (orders.order_items). NULL = order-level or account-level charge (shipping, rush, adjustment). · → orders.order_items
invoice_idbiginton delete restrictInvoice the charge was billed on, when known at insert time (billing.invoices). The row is append-only, so a charge invoiced later is linked through billing.invoice_lines.charge_id instead. NULL = not invoiced when recorded. · → billing.invoices
charge_kindcharacter varying(30)not nullWhat was charged: 'service' = design/planning/production service on an order item; 'product' = physical good or licence; 'shipping' = shipping fee; 'rush' = rush (expedite) fee; 'adjustment' = manual correction, either sign; 'credit' = reversal or goodwill credit to the client (negative); 'refund' = reversal of a charge whose money was returned (negative). · default 'service'::character varying
reverses_charge_idbiginton delete restrictThe original charge this row reverses (uncharge). Only credit/refund rows may carry it; partial reversals are allowed, so several rows may reverse one charge. NULL = not a reversal (an original charge, or a credit not tied to one charge). · → billing.charges
currency_codecore.currency_codeFINANCIALnot null on delete restrictCurrency of amount (core.currencies). [FINANCIAL] · → core.currencies
amountcore.money_amountFINANCIALnot nullSigned amount in currency_code: >= 0 for service/product/shipping/rush (0 only for a zero-charge item with a zero-charge reason on the order item), < 0 for credit/refund, non-zero either sign for adjustment. SUM(amount) is the net charge. [FINANCIAL]
charged_ondatenot nullBusiness date of the charge (the day the item was charged), used for daily charge reports; defaults to today. · default CURRENT_DATE
is_manualbooleannot nulltrue = entered by a staff member by hand; false = written by the charging process when an order item reached its charge point. · default false
reasoncharacter varying(255)PHI-RISKWhy the charge or reversal was made (required in practice for manual rows and uncharges; enforced by V100). User input; may name a patient by mistake. NULL = automatic charge with no reason needed. [PHI-RISK]

created_attimestamp with time zoneAUDITnot nullUTC instant the charge row was recorded. [AUDIT] · default now()

uq_charges__uuidUNIQUEUNIQUE (uuid)The public uuid identifies exactly one charge.

ck_charges__charge_kindCHECKCHECK (((charge_kind)::text = ANY ((ARRAY['service'::character varying, 'product'::character varying, 'shipping'::character varying, 'rush'::character varying, 'adjustment'::character varying, 'credit'::character varying, 'refund'::character varying])::text[])))Charge kind is one of the documented values.
ck_charges__not_self_reversalCHECKCHECK (((reverses_charge_id IS NULL) OR (reverses_charge_id <> id)))A charge cannot reverse itself.

billing.payment_methods

PIISECRET-REFAUDITV020 rls forced · tenant isolation audited traceable to legacy 23 columns
A client's stored way to pay: a tokenised card, bank transfer, cheque, cash, credit balance or third-party payer. Cards are held only as a gateway vault/processor token reference plus brand, last four digits and expiry for recognition: the card number (PAN) and CVV are NEVER stored in this database (out of PCI scope; legacy UserAcounts.CreditCard is deliberately not migrated). At most one default active method per client (iSmileOn payment method requirement). Lifecycle: deactivated (is_active=false), never deleted while payments reference it. Contains PII. [FINANCIAL]

display_labelcharacter varying(120)Masked label shown to users, e.g. "VISA ****1019"; never contains more than the last four digits. Migrated from UserAcounts.CardType + last four. NULL = no label (method recognised by kind only).
processor_codecharacter varying(40)Payment gateway holding the vault token: 'versapay', 'cybersource', 'skyline', 'quickbooks', 'other'. Migrated from the UserAcounts vault column that was filled (VersaPayVaultID, CybersourceBillRekID/BillRek, SkyLineVaultID). NULL = no gateway (non-card method or card without token).
provider_tokencharacter varying(255)PIISECRET-REFOpaque vault/processor token reference issued by the gateway (processor_code) and used to charge the card. Money received from (or returned to) a client through the gateway, bank or by hand. One row = one payment transaction; applied to invoices through billing.payment_allocations. docs

10 tables · 165 columns

Files and configurable documents: file metadata, upload records and links, document templates, versioned document records (forms, fabrication notes, instruction sheets), text snippets.

File metadata and configurable documents. docs.document_records are versioned regulated records (version_no, state, supersedes_id, content_hash); migrated legacy forms load as migrated — immutable, but not claiming an approval that never happened. document_links ties a file to whatever it belongs to.

docs.document_records

PHIAUDITV021 rls forced · tenant isolation audited traceable to legacy 24 columns
One version of a filled-in form (fabrication notes, SG instruction sheet, confirmation form, prosthetic protocol) for an order, order item, production job or surgical kit protocol: a regulated record under 21 CFR Part 11 / 820 (V3_DESIGN C6). Versioned: version_no, state draft -> in_review -> approved -> superseded, supersedes_id, content_hash. An approved or superseded version is immutable (trg_document_records__immutable_when_approved); a correction inserts a new version that supersedes it. At most one approved and one open (draft/in_review) version per (template, order item). Answers are rows in docs.document_record_values; electronic signatures reference (record, version_no, content_hash) in compliance.electronic_signatures. legacy_source names the legacy form table. Contains PHI (clinical free text and tooth-level details tied to a patient's order).

docs.documents

PHIPHI-RISKAUDITV021 rls forced · tenant isolation traceable to legacy 29 columns
One stored file (an upload or a generated document): metadata only, the bytes live in object storage under storage_key. Merges legacy ServiceFiles, IsmileFiles, caseDocuments and the file columns of the order tables. Uploads are first-class records (D3 §X2): each has a purpose, an upload_status lifecycle, a SHA-256 integrity hash and the channel it arrived through; docs.document_links attaches one upload to several orders, order items or cases. Versions: a replacement file is a new row with supersedes_id. Soft-deleted (deleted_at). Owned by the docs module. Contains PHI (clinical scans and photos; file names often carry the patient name).

comms.email_logs

PHI-RISKPIIV022 partitioned RANGE (sent_at) · 35 rls forced · tenant isolation audited traceable to legacy 25 columns
One email sent (or queued/attempted) by the system: recipients, subject, delivery status, and what it was about. Migrated from legacy Mail_log (~4.9 M rows; no order reference in the source, so order_id is NULL for migrated rows). Range-partitioned on sent_at: pre-2017 bucket, yearly 2017-2025, monthly from 2026, DEFAULT for strays; the primary key includes sent_at. Rows are written once and then only their delivery fields (status, delivered_at, opened_at, error_message) change from provider webhooks; never edited otherwise. Retention by dropping old partitions (policy TO CONFIRM, Q6). Contains PII (addresses) and PHI-RISK (subjects such as "Order # 6256 - <patient>").

comms.email_suppressions

PIIAUDITV022 rls forced · tenant isolation audited traceable to legacy 17 columns
Deliverability / suppression list consulted before sending: one row per address per tenant with its latest status (bounced, complained, unsubscribed, invalid). Migrated from SESemail.json (13,494 {email, status} records; includes synthetic smilesourcetempemail.ddx placeholders and spam sign-ups) and fed afterwards by SES bounce/complaint webhooks and unsubscribe links. A sent email to a suppressed address is logged with status 'suppressed'. Released (released_at), not deleted. Contains PII.

Sending is blocked for every value except 'deliverable'. comms.notification_rules

AUDITV022 rls forced · tenant isolation traceable to legacy 22 columns
Which trigger sends which template on which channel (D3 §X3): exactly one trigger (an application event code, entering a workflow state, or taking a workflow transition), optionally narrowed to one sellable item or catalog category and to one client/DSO, sending one email template (or an in-app/push message). integration

8 tables · 133 columns

Boundary to external systems (iSmile, Relu, Vulcan, Planmeca, Medit, QuickBooks, SES, InsightHub and others): providers, accounts, external references, sync runs, webhooks, transfer tasks.

The boundary for external systems. A business table never carries a third-party identifier; integration.external_references does. Webhooks are idempotent per provider; transfer_tasks is the Relu task dock (upload / download / AI).

integration.accounts

SECRET-REFAUDITV023 rls forced · tenant isolation audited traceable to legacy 17 columns
A tenant's (or one client's) account with an external provider: the 3DDX QuickBooks company, the FedEx shipper account, a doctor's Medit or OV account. One row per (tenant, provider, label). Holds identifiers and non-secret settings only; credentials live in AWS SSM Parameter Store and are referenced by name in credential_ref. Deactivated rather than deleted (sync runs and references point at it).
columntypetags · constraintsmeaning
idbigintpkSurrogate key. Referenced by external_references and sync_runs.

integration.external_references

AUDITV023 rls forced · tenant isolation traceable to legacy 19 columns
The one link between a local record and its counterpart in an external system: an order's Vulcan id, an order item's Relu order id and viewer URL, a client's OV licence, an iSmile order number, a QuickBooks invoice id. Replaces the scattered legacy columns (IsmileID, vulcanRef, quickbooksId …) on business tables. entity_type + entity_id is a polymorphic reference (no FK, the target table depends on entity_type); the application and V100 functions resolve it. Updated as syncs run; detached rather than deleted when the remote record goes away.
columntypetags · constraintsmeaning
idbigintpkSurrogate key, system-generated identity; not shown to users.
tenant_idbigintnot null on delete restrictOwning tenant (core.tenants; FK added in V090), the tenant of the referenced local record. Defaults to the session tenant app.tenant_id: the ETL inserts without naming it and runs inside the tenant context. · → core.tenants · default core.fn_current_tenant()
provider_idbigintnot null on delete restrictExternal system the id belongs to (integration.providers). · → integration.providers
account_idbiginton delete cascadeProvider account the record lives under, when the provider has several (integration.accounts). NULL = the provider has one namespace for the tenant. · → integration.accounts
entity_typecharacter varying(40)not nullKind of local record entity_id points to: 'order' = orders.orders; 'order_item' = orders.order_items (Relu AI plan, iSmile sub-order); 'case' = orders.cases; 'contact' = crm.contacts (OV licence); 'patient' = clinical.patients; 'user' = iam.users (a member of staff named by an integration); 'invoice' / 'payment' = billing; 'shipment' = shipping.shipments; 'document' = docs.documents; 'production_job' = production.production_jobs; 'voucher' = vouchers.vouchers; 'sellable_item' = catalog.sellable_items; 'implant_manufacturer' / 'implant_system' / 'surgical_kit' / 'sleeve_system' = clinical implant-library rows matched to the Relu implant library (D3 §14).
entity_idbigintnot nullId of the local record in the table named by entity_type. Polymorphic: no FK; integrity is checked by the reconciliation stage and V100 functions.
external_idcharacter varying(255)not nullThe provider's identifier for the record (Relu order id, Vulcan id, QuickBooks id, OV licence id). Migrated from the legacy column of the business table (e.g. VulcanSGData.vulcanID, OV_Licence.License_ID).

legacy_sourcecharacter varying(64)Legacy table the link was migrated from (VulcanSGData, OV_Licence, Orders.IsmileID …). NULL = created in threeddx3 or not recorded by the ETL.
legacy_keycharacter varying(200)Composite legacy key when one id does not identify the source row. NULL = legacy_id alone identifies it, or not migrated.
created_attimestamp with time zoneAUDITnot nullWhen the link was recorded, UTC instant. System-generated. [AUDIT] · default now()
updated_attimestamp with time zoneAUDITnot nullWhen the link last changed, UTC instant; set by trg_external_references__touch_updated_at. [AUDIT] · default now()

integration.providers

AUDITV023 traceable to legacy 15 columns
External systems 3DDX exchanges data with: iSmile, Vulcan, Planmeca, Medit, Exocad, QuickBooks, VersaPay, CyberSource, FedEx, Mailchimp, InsightHub, OV, SES, S3, Pusher, Relu, Vatech, Straumann, TreatPlan AI and others. One row per system. Global (no tenant_id): a provider is the same system for every tenant; what is tenant-specific (credentials, account ids, settings) lives in integration.accounts. Seeded in V2nn; rows are deactivated, never deleted, because references and logs point at them.

idbigintpkSurrogate key. Referenced by accounts, external_references, sync_runs, webhook_events, api_requests, transfer_tasks, shipping.couriers and compliance.business_associates.

integration.transfer_tasks

PHI-RISKAUDITV023 rls forced · tenant isolation traceable to legacy 23 columns
Relu Task Dock (D3 §14, Relu Viewer Integration v2.0 US#8–10): the server-side record of a long-running transfer for an order item, the source of truth the Connect UI shows on every device and tab. One row per order and task type (task_key = '{orderId}-{type}'): 'upload' = scans sent to S3 / Relu (CBCT only goes to Relu); 'download' = a plan or export fetched for the client; 'ai' = the Relu AI planning job. A retry reuses the row (failed → uploading, attempts + 1). Transition rules (no regressions, illegal transitions rejected) are enforced by a V100/V110 business trigger, not here. Rows of old orders are cleaned up by the platform job.

idbigintpkSurrogate key, system-generated identity; not shown to users.

directioncharacter varying(20)not nullTask type: 'upload' = files leaving the client for S3 / Relu; 'download' = a file prepared for the client to download; 'ai' = the Relu AI planning job, shown only after its upload completed.
statuscharacter varying(20)not nullTask state (D3 §14 task model; 'queued' and 'manual' were dropped in v2.0): 'uploading' = upload in progress (also after a retry); 'downloading' = download in progress; 'processing' = Relu AI job running; 'ready' = AI plan ready to view; 'completed' = upload or download finished (progress 100); 'cancelled' = stopped by the user; 'failed' = gave up after retries, or AI failed / timed out after 1 h (the TP falls back to manual planning); 'archived' = AI plan set aside after the clinic chose FT session or amendment. Allowed per direction: upload {uploading, completed, cancelled, failed}; download {downloading, completed, cancelled, failed}; ai {processing, ready, failed, archived}.

integration.webhook_events

PIIV023 rls forced · tenant isolation audited traceable to legacy 16 columns
Inbound events pushed by providers: SES delivery / bounce / complaint / engagement notifications (12M+ migrated rows from SESDeliveryNotifications, SESEmailNotifications, SESEngagementNotifications) and live Relu order.job_status callbacks. One row per received delivery; stored before processing so a crash never loses an event. Idempotency: migrated rows are unique on their legacy source row (v2 V045: a provider message id is not an event id), live rows on (tenant, provider, idempotency_key) so a redelivered webhook is recognised and marked 'duplicate'. Only signature-verified events may be processed (D4 rule 18). Payloads can contain email addresses and order data. Contains PII.

idbigintpkSurrogate key, system-generated identity; not shown to users.
tenant_idbigintnot null on delete restrictTenant the event concerns (core.tenants; FK added in V090), resolved from the endpoint/account the provider called. Defaults to the session tenant app.tenant_id (the ETL inserts without naming it). · → core.tenants · default core.fn_current_tenant()
provider_idbigintnot null on delete restrictProvider that sent the event (integration.providers). · → integration.providers

external_event_idcharacter varying(255)The provider's id for the message or object the event concerns (SES message id, Relu job id). Not unique: one message produces a delivery, then opens and clicks, each its own row. NULL = the provider sent no such id.
idempotency_keycharacter varying(255)Unique delivery id of a live event (provider delivery id header, or a hash of provider + event id + status when the provider gives none), used to detect redeliveries. NULL = migrated row (identified by legacy_source + legacy_id instead) or a provider that cannot supply one.
signature_validbooleannot nulltrue = the request signature or shared-secret authentication was verified on receipt. false = not verified, failed, or the row was migrated (legacy tables kept no signature evidence). Live events with false are never processed (ck_webhook_events__process_only_signed); Relu's endpoint is public, so this is its only authentication. · default false

statuscharacter varying(20)not nullProcessing state: 'received' = stored, not yet handled; 'processing' = a worker holds it; 'processed' = applied to local records; 'failed' = handling errored, will be retried (attempts); 'ignored' = valid but deliberately not applied (provider inactive, callback after the order was archived, unsigned or corrupt payload); 'duplicate' = a redelivery of an event already received. · default 'received'::character varying
attemptssmallintnot nullNumber of processing attempts so far; 0 = not yet tried. System-generated. · default 0

processed_attimestamp with time zoneWhen processing finished (processed, ignored or duplicate), UTC instant. NULL = not finished.
legacy_idbigintPrimary key of the legacy SES notification row. With legacy_source it identifies a migrated event, because the provider message id does not. NULL = live event.

definition
 SELECT ch.tenant_id,
    ch.charged_on AS revenue_date,
    ch.currency_code,
    ch.charge_kind,
    cat.code AS category_code,
    count(DISTINCT ch.order_id) AS order_count,
    count(*) AS charge_count,
    sum(ch.amount::numeric) AS gross_amount
   FROM billing.charges ch
     LEFT JOIN orders.order_items oi ON oi.id = ch.order_item_id
     LEFT JOIN catalog.sellable_items si ON si.id = oi.sellable_item_id
     LEFT JOIN catalog.categories cat ON cat.id = si.category_id
  GROUP BY ch.tenant_id, ch.charged_on, ch.currency_code, ch.charge_kind, cat.code;

reporting.mv_monthly_volume

materialized view 9 columns
Orders, items, redos, value and active clients per tenant, month, category and item kind, for trend reporting (value summed across currencies as stored). Never granted directly — read reporting.v_monthly_volume.
columntypemeaning
tenant_idbigint
monthdate
category_codecore.entity_code
item_kindcatalog.item_kind
order_countbigint
item_countbigint
redo_countbigint
total_valuenumeric
active_clientsbigint
definition
 SELECT o.tenant_id,
    date_trunc('month'::text, o.created_at)::date AS month,
    cat.code AS category_code,
    si.item_kind,
    count(DISTINCT o.id) AS order_count,
    count(oi.id) AS item_count,
    count(oi.id) FILTER (WHERE oi.is_redo) AS redo_count,
    sum(oi.line_total::numeric) AS total_value,
    count(DISTINCT o.contact_id) AS active_clients
   FROM orders.orders o
     JOIN orders.order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.id AND oi.deleted_at IS NULL
     JOIN catalog.sellable_items si ON si.id = oi.sellable_item_id
     LEFT JOIN catalog.categories cat ON cat.id = si.category_id
  WHERE o.deleted_at IS NULL AND NOT o.is_testing
  GROUP BY o.tenant_id, (date_trunc('month'::text, o.created_at)::date), cat.code, si.item_kind;

reporting.v_client_activity

view · security_invoker=true 15 columns
Per client: order counts and value (lifetime and last 12 months), first/last order, never-ordered and dormant (no order for 12 months) flags — the "inactive clients" and "clients to service" questions. Totals are summed across currencies as stored; convert before comparing clients in different currencies. Excludes test and placeholder contacts.
columntypemeaning
contact_idbigint
tenant_idbigint
display_namecharacter varying(255)
contact_typecharacter varying(30)
registered_attimestamp with time zone
first_order_attimestamp with time zone
last_order_attimestamp with time zone
sales_rep_namecharacter varying(255)
country_namecharacter varying(150)
order_countbigint
orders_last_12mbigint
lifetime_valuenumeric
value_last_12mnumeric
never_orderedboolean
dormantboolean
definition
 SELECT c.id AS contact_id,
    c.tenant_id,
    c.display_name,
    c.contact_type,
    c.registered_at,
    c.first_order_at,
    c.last_order_at,
    rep.display_name AS sales_rep_name,
    co.name AS country_name,
    count(o.id) AS order_count,
    count(o.id) FILTER (WHERE o.created_at >= (now() - '1 year'::interval)) AS orders_last_12m,
    COALESCE(sum(o.total_amount::numeric), 0::numeric) AS lifetime_value,
    COALESCE(sum(o.total_amount::numeric) FILTER (WHERE o.created_at >= (now() - '1 year'::interval)), 0::numeric) AS value_last_12m,
    c.last_order_at IS NULL AS never_ordered,
    c.last_order_at IS NOT NULL AND c.last_order_at < (now() - '1 year'::interval) AS dormant
   FROM crm.contacts c
     LEFT JOIN orders.orders o ON o.contact_id = c.id AND o.deleted_at IS NULL
     LEFT JOIN iam.users rep ON rep.id = c.sales_rep_user_id
     LEFT JOIN core.countries co ON co.id = c.country_id
  WHERE c.deleted_at IS NULL AND NOT c.is_testing AND NOT c.is_placeholder
  GROUP BY c.id, c.tenant_id, c.display_name, c.contact_type, c.registered_at, c.first_order_at, c.last_order_at, rep.display_name, co.name;

 SELECT oi.id AS order_item_id,
    o.id AS order_id,
    o.tenant_id,
    o.case_id,
    o.order_number,
    o.order_reference,
    o.status AS order_status,

    oi.item_role,
    oi.restoration_stage,

    si.name AS item_name,
    si.item_kind,
    cat.code AS category_code,

    c.display_name AS client_name,
    c.contact_type,
    sc.id AS scan_center_id,
    sc.display_name AS scan_center_name,
    rep.display_name AS sales_rep_name,
    p.patient_code,
    oi.currency_code,
    oi.unit_price,
    oi.fields_amount,
    oi.discount_amount,
    oi.voucher_amount,
    oi.line_total,
    oi.is_billable,
    oi.is_invoiced,
    oi.is_digital,
    oi.is_redo,
    oi.hold_type,
    o.priority,
    o.surgery_date,
    o.created_at AS order_created_at,
    o.submitted_at,
    oi.sent_to_production_at,
    oi.completed_at AS item_completed_at,
    oi.closed_at AS item_closed_at,
    designer.display_name AS designer_name,
    operator.display_name AS operator_name
   FROM orders.order_items oi
     JOIN orders.orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id
     JOIN catalog.sellable_items si ON si.id = oi.sellable_item_id

     LEFT JOIN iam.users designer ON designer.id = oi.designer_user_id
     LEFT JOIN iam.users operator ON operator.id = oi.operator_user_id
  WHERE oi.deleted_at IS NULL AND o.deleted_at IS NULL;

reporting.v_production_pipeline

view · security_invoker=true 9 columns
Open work by category and status for the operations dashboard: item count, overdue count, oldest item and average age in days.
columntypemeaning
tenant_idbigint
category_codecore.entity_code
category_namecharacter varying(150)
item_kindcatalog.item_kind
item_statuscharacter varying(50)
item_countbigint
overdue_countbigint
oldest_created_attimestamp with time zone
avg_age_daysnumeric(10,2)
definition
 SELECT oi.tenant_id,
    cat.code AS category_code,
    cat.name AS category_name,
    si.item_kind,
    oi.status AS item_status,
    count(*) AS item_count,
    count(*) FILTER (WHERE oi.due_at < now()) AS overdue_count,
    min(oi.created_at) AS oldest_created_at,
    avg(EXTRACT(epoch FROM now() - oi.created_at) / 86400::numeric)::numeric(10,2) AS avg_age_days
   FROM orders.order_items oi
     JOIN catalog.sellable_items si ON si.id = oi.sellable_item_id
     LEFT JOIN catalog.categories cat ON cat.id = si.category_id
  WHERE oi.deleted_at IS NULL AND (oi.status::text <> ALL (ARRAY['completed'::character varying, 'cancelled'::character varying, 'delivered'::character varying]::text[]))
  GROUP BY oi.tenant_id, cat.code, cat.name, si.item_kind, oi.status;

reporting.v_voucher_balances

view · security_invoker=true 21 columns
Voucher position for the expiry and credit questions: every balance column, remaining cases, and an expiry bucket (no_expiry, expired, expiring_soon = within 90 days, active).
columntypemeaning

client_namecharacter varying(255)

currency_codecore.currency_code
issued_creditcore.money_amount

definition
 SELECT v.id AS voucher_id,
    v.tenant_id,
    v.voucher_code,
    vt.code AS voucher_type_code,
    vt.name AS voucher_type_name,
    vt.credit_kind,
    c.display_name AS client_name,
    v.status,
    v.currency_code,
    v.issued_credit,
    v.consumed_credit,
    v.expired_credit,
    v.refunded_credit,
    v.remaining_credit,
    v.issued_cases,
    v.consumed_cases,
    v.expired_cases,
    v.issued_cases - v.consumed_cases - v.expired_cases AS remaining_cases,
    v.issued_on,
    v.expires_on,
        CASE
            WHEN v.expires_on IS NULL THEN 'no_expiry'::text
            WHEN v.expires_on < CURRENT_DATE THEN 'expired'::text
            WHEN v.expires_on < (CURRENT_DATE + 90) THEN 'expiring_soon'::text
            ELSE 'active'::text
        END AS expiry_bucket
   FROM vouchers.vouchers v
     JOIN vouchers.voucher_types vt ON vt.id = v.voucher_type_id
     LEFT JOIN crm.contacts c ON c.id = v.contact_id;

compliance

HIPAA, GDPR and FDA 21 CFR 820/Part 11 as data: classifications, consents, subject requests, restrictions, legal holds, retention, disclosures, business associates, incidents, CAPA, controlled documents, electronic signatures, traceability, UDI.

HIPAA, GDPR and FDA 21 CFR Part 11 / 820 as data: data classifications (which column is PHI / PII), consents, subject requests, processing restrictions, legal holds, versioned retention policies (inactive until approved), disclosure rules, business associates, electronic signatures that pin the exact record version and hash, trace links (the device history record graph), UDI assignments and break-glass sessions.

compliance.authorizations

PHIPHI-RISKAUDITV025 rls forced · tenant isolation audited traceable to legacy 25 columns
Signed HIPAA authorizations (HIPAA-Pr-02-01: a client authorises sending a case to another doctor, publication of photographs, research use) and v2-era GDPR consent forms. One row per signed authorization; revocable, and revocation stops future use but not disclosures already made. GDPR consent captured through the portals is recorded in compliance.consents; this table holds the signed-form authorizations. Contains PHI.

compliance.break_glass_sessions

PHIPHI-RISKPIIAUDITV025 rls forced · tenant isolation audited 17 columns
Emergency ("break-glass") access sessions (C1, HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(ii) emergency access procedure): a person bypasses normal PHI restrictions (e.g. reads patient identity without the usual purpose, or an admin acts with BYPASSRLS) and must state why. One row per session: who, why, which patient if one, when it started and ended, and who approved or reviewed it (approval may come after the fact). Every PHI read inside the session is still logged in audit.phi_access_log, and the session start/end in audit.event_log. Contains PHI.

compliance.consents

PIIAUDITV025 rls forced · tenant isolation append-only traceable to legacy 23 columns
GDPR consent and lawful-basis records (C5, Art. 6/7/9): which data subject (a client contact or a patient — never both) agreed to which purpose, on which basis, when, through which channel, with what evidence, and when they withdrew. History semantics: a row is one grant and is never deleted or rewritten. Giving consent inserts a row; withdrawing sets withdrawn_at and withdrawal_via on that row once (the only permitted update — enforced by a V110 business trigger; DELETE is rejected here); consenting again inserts a new row. The ordered rows for a subject and purpose are therefore the complete consent history Art. 7(1) requires the controller to demonstrate. At most one open (unwithdrawn) row per subject and purpose. Contains PII.

compliance.data_classifications

PHI-RISKAUDITV025 13 columns
Machine-readable map of where regulated data lives, one row per classified column of threeddx3. Drives PHI redaction in audit.audit_log (C4), the anonymiser for non-production copies (threeddx3_anony), de-identified exports (HIPAA-Pr-11, the 18 identifiers) and the answer to "what personal data do you hold about me?". Global (no tenant_id) on purpose: it describes the database schema, which is the same for every tenant. Seeded in V2nn; tools/check_data_classifications.py verifies every named column exists.

compliance.destruction_events

AUDITV025 rls forced · tenant isolation traceable to legacy 21 columns
The Destruction Log (HIPAA-Pr-05-01): every destruction of records, models or devices — what, how many, which period, when, how, by whom, witnessed by whom, under which retention policy version. compliance.electronic_signatures

PIIAUDITSNAPSHOTV025 rls forced · tenant isolation append-only traceable to legacy 21 columns
Electronic signatures under 21 CFR Part 11 (11.50, 11.70, 11.100, 11.200) on regulated records — design approvals (orders.order_item_decisions), forms and prescriptions (docs.document_records), QC inspections, production reports, UDI records, controlled-document revisions, surgical kit protocols. Each signature shows the signer's printed name, date/time and meaning, and is linked to the exact record version and its content hash at signing, so it cannot be excised, copied or transferred to another record or version. The record reference is polymorphic (schema, table, id, version; no FK — the target table varies), verified by V100 functions. Append-only: never updated or deleted; a withdrawn approval is a new 'rejected' signature or a new record version.

compliance.legal_holds

AUDITV025 rls forced · tenant isolation audited traceable to legacy 27 columns
Legal holds (C5, Q6 "legal-hold support"): an instruction that records about a client, patient, case, order, document, a described record set or the whole tenant must be preserved because of litigation, investigation, an audit or a complaint. While a hold is active (released_at NULL) compliance.fn_erase_contact refuses erasure and the retention sweep refuses destruction of covered records, recording the exception; this overrides any retention policy and any erasure request. One row per hold; released, never deleted.

PHIPHI-RISKPIIAUDITV025 rls forced · tenant isolation append-only traceable to legacy 26 columns
Accounting of disclosures (HIPAA-Pr-03-02, 45 CFR 164.528): every disclosure of PHI outside 3DDX — sending a case to a partner lab, a design to another doctor, files to Relu — with when, what, to whom, why and under which permission, producible for six years on demand. is_accountable is false for treatment, payment and operations, which are exempt from the accounting but still recorded. compliance.retention_policies

AUDITV025 rls forced · tenant isolation audited traceable to legacy 26 columns
Retention schedule (HIPAA-Pr-05; FDA device-record retention; GDPR storage limitation), managed as controlled, versioned configuration (Q6): per record type, how long, from which start event, under which legal basis and jurisdiction, effective when, approved by whom. One row per policy version; a change inserts version_no + 1 and ends the previous version's effective period. A policy can drive deletion only while is_active, and is_active requires an approval, a period and an effective date. TO CONFIRM (Q6): the actual periods and start events await QMS/Privacy/Legal approval, so every seeded policy is inactive and the retention sweep only lists candidates; legal holds (compliance.legal_holds) override any policy.

PIIAUDITV025 rls forced · tenant isolation audited traceable to legacy 25 columns
Data-subject requests under HIPAA-Pr-03 (individual rights) and GDPR Chapter III: access, copy, amendment/rectification, restriction, accounting of disclosures, portability, erasure, objection. One register because the kinds overlap and the deadline is what matters. One row per request; kept after closure as evidence of compliance. The request survives erasure of its subject (subject links are SET NULL, requester_name stays). Contains PII.

compliance.trace_links

AUDITV025 rls forced · tenant isolation append-only 9 columns
Device history record graph (C6, 21 CFR 820 DHR / ISO 13485 7.5.9 traceability): directed edges "from entity → to entity" connecting a case and its order items to the input documents (scans), design versions, approvals and their signatures, operators, production jobs and reports, QC inspections, surgical kit protocols, UDI assignments and shipments. Walking forward from an input answers "which devices used this scan"; walking backward from a UDI answers "everything that went into this device". Entities are polymorphic (type + id, no FK; resolved by V100 functions). Pure link table, append-only: an edge recorded in error is answered by a new edge, not removed.
columntypetags · constraintsmeaning
idbigintpkSurrogate key of the edge; not shown to users.
tenant_idbigintnot null on delete restrictOwning tenant (core.tenants; FK added in V090). Defaults to the session tenant app.tenant_id. · → core.tenants · default core.fn_current_tenant()
from_entity_typecharacter varying(40)not nullKind of the source node: 'case' (orders.cases), 'order', 'order_item' (orders), 'document' (docs.documents), 'document_record' (docs.document_records, a form/design version), 'order_item_decision' (design approval), 'production_job', 'production_report' (production), 'quality_inspection' (quality.inspections), 'electronic_signature', 'udi_assignment' (compliance), 'serialised_unit' (inventory), 'shipment' (shipping), 'surgical_kit_protocol' (clinical), 'user' (iam.users, an operator).
from_entity_idbigintnot nullId of the source node in the table named by from_entity_type (polymorphic, no FK).
to_entity_typecharacter varying(40)not nullKind of the target node; same vocabulary as from_entity_type.
to_entity_idbigintnot nullId of the target node in the table named by to_entity_type (polymorphic, no FK).
link_kindcharacter varying(30)not nullMeaning of the edge, read "from <kind> to": 'input_to' = a scan/document was an input to an item or design; 'design_for' = a design version was made for an order item; 'approval_of' = a decision approves a design/record; 'signature_of' = a signature authenticates a record; 'produced_by' = a unit/item was produced by a job; 'operated_by' = a job/step was performed by a user; 'inspected_by' = a job/unit was checked by an inspection; 'labelled_as' = a unit/item received a UDI; 'shipped_in' = a unit/item left in a shipment; 'uses_protocol' = a design/item uses a surgical kit protocol version; 'derived_from' = a record was derived from another (refinement, redo); 'supersedes' = a version replaces another.
created_attimestamp with time zoneAUDITnot nullWhen the edge was recorded, UTC instant. [AUDIT] · default now()
created_by_user_idbigintAUDITiam.users.id of the person whose action recorded the edge. No FK by design (audit history). NULL = recorded by the system. [AUDIT]

compliance.udi_assignments

AUDITV025 rls forced · tenant isolation audited traceable to legacy 28 columns
UDI production identifiers: one row per version of the UDI label data of one physical device released (patient-matched surgical guide, Night Guard): DI + lot/serial, manufacturing and expiry dates, encoded carrier string and label revision, linked to the order item, production job, serialised unit and shipment. Answers both directions of a recall (which devices came from this build; which build produced this UDI). Regulated record (C6, 21 CFR 830 / 820): versioned with state draft → in_review → approved → superseded, content_hash at approval, and immutable once approved (trg_udi_assignments__immutable_when_approved); a reprint with corrected data is a new version with supersedes_id.

Functions

functionreturnsexecute granted tobehaviour
fn_erase_contact(p_contact_id bigint, p_subject_request_id bigint)jsonbsecurity definer
app_rw, owner
GDPR Art. 17 erasure for a client contact of the current tenant, given an open identity-verified erasure subject request: anonymises the contact, its addresses and its login in place, deletes its e-mail and phone rows, archives and soft-deletes the contact and login, and logs record_deleted to audit.event_log. Refused while a legal hold blocking erasure covers the contact or tenant. Orders, invoices, charges and regulated records are kept because law requires them (retention exception), but no longer identify the person. Closing the subject request is the caller's step.
fn_export_subject(p_contact_id bigint, p_subject_request_id bigint)jsonbsecurity definer
app_rw, owner
GDPR Art. 15 / 20: returns, as one JSON document, the personal data held about a client contact (contact record, login identity, addresses, e-mails, phones, preferences, consents, order summary) for an open access/copy/portability subject request of the current tenant. Patient health data is not included (the client is the data subject here; patients' requests go through the clinic as controller). Logged as data_export in audit.event_log.

audit

9 tables · 103 columns · 4 functions

Tamper-evident trails: row-change audit log (hash-chained), application event log, PHI access log, and the migration's own run, id-map, exclusion and reconciliation records.

Tamper-evident trails. audit.audit_log is monthly partitioned and hash-chained (audit.fn_verify_chain recomputes it); event_log records logins, exports, signatures and break-glass; phi_access_log records every PHI read through a function. The migration's own trail lives here too: run records, id map, the exclusion ledger and reconciliation results.

audit.audit_log

PHIPHI-RISKPIIAUDITV005 partitioned RANGE (occurred_at) · 25 rls forced · tenant isolation append-only 19 columns
Tamper-evident trail of every row change on PHI, financial and regulated tables (HIPAA 164.312(b), 21 CFR Part 11 audit trail): one row per INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE of an audited row, or per TRUNCATE. Written only by the trigger function core.fn_audit_row() (V140); PHI columns are replaced by "[redacted]" in the before/after images using compliance.data_classifications. Hash-chained (row_hash = sha256(prev_hash || canonical row), serialised by an advisory lock) so any edit or deletion is detectable by audit.fn_verify_chain. Append-only: UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE are rejected by trigger; old months are detached, archived and dropped by partition maintenance only. Partitioned by month on occurred_at. Contains PHI-RISK (free-text values in the images that the redaction list does not cover).
columntypetags · constraintsmeaning
idbigintpkSurrogate key, always generated (GENERATED ALWAYS) so an audit row cannot be written with a chosen id. Unique together with occurred_at (partition key).
occurred_attimestamp with time zonepkUTC instant of the change (transaction time of the audited statement). Partition key.
tenant_idbigintTenant in whose session the change was made (app.tenant_id). No FK by design: history survives the tenant. NULL = change to a global table (e.g. core.currencies) or made outside any tenant session (migration, maintenance by an administrator).
actor_user_idbigintAUDITiam.users.id of the person who made the change (app.user_id). No FK by design: history survives the user. NULL = system job, migration or a direct database session without app.user_id; db_role then says who. [AUDIT]
actor_role_idbigintAUDITiam.roles.id the person was acting in (app.role_id), answering "who, in which role". No FK by design. NULL = no application role set (system, migration, direct database session). [AUDIT]
db_rolecharacter varying(63)AUDITnot nullPostgreSQL role that executed the statement (current_user, e.g. 'app', 'aya', 'threeddx3_etl'). Distinguishes application traffic from administrators working directly in the database. [AUDIT] · default CURRENT_USER
actioncharacter varying(20)not nullWhat happened: 'INSERT' = row created (new_values only); 'UPDATE' = row changed (old and new images, changed_columns); 'DELETE' = row removed (old_values only); 'TRUNCATE' = whole table emptied (no images, record_id NULL).
schema_namecharacter varying(63)not nullSchema of the audited table, e.g. 'billing'.
table_namecharacter varying(63)not nullName of the audited table, e.g. 'invoices'.
record_idbigintValue of the audited row's id column. NULL = TRUNCATE, or a table whose key is not a bigint id (e.g. core.currencies keyed by code; the key is then in old_values/new_values).

new_valuesjsonbPHI-RISKRow image after the change as JSON, PHI columns redacted. NULL = DELETE or TRUNCATE (no new image). [PHI-RISK]
changed_columnstext[]Names of the columns whose value differs between old_values and new_values, for fast "who changed the price?" queries. NULL = not an UPDATE.

audit.event_log

PIIAUDITV005 partitioned RANGE (occurred_at) · 25 rls forced · tenant isolation append-only 16 columns
Security and compliance events that are not row changes: logins and failed logins, logouts, password events, permission and role changes, data exports, deletions, break-glass access, consent changes, electronic-signature events and bulk PHI reads. One row per event, written by the application and by V100/V140 functions. Append-only (UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE rejected by trigger); partitioned by month on occurred_at; old months leave by partition maintenance only. details never holds PHI or secrets (no passwords, tokens or patient identifiers).

audit.migration_exclusions

V005 10 columns
Exclusion ledger: every legacy row a run deliberately did not migrate, with the reason and the approval, so reconciliation can prove source = migrated + approved exclusions with zero unexplained rows (design E10). One row per excluded source row per run. Examples: 1,394 children of deleted parents (Q21), OrderTrn/OrderOrtho and offer50 retired tables (Q21/Q18), UserSessions excluded for security (U3). GLOBAL table (no tenant_id). details never holds PHI. Kept permanently as migration evidence; only approval_reference is filled in later.
columntypetags · constraintsmeaning
idbigintpkSurrogate key of the exclusion row.
run_iduuidnot null on delete restrictRun that excluded the row. FK to audit.migration_runs. · → audit.migration_runs
legacy_tablecharacter varying(80)not nullLegacy MySQL table of the excluded row, e.g. 'OrderTrn'.
legacy_idbigintNumeric id of the excluded source row. NULL = the source row has no single numeric id; legacy_key identifies it.
legacy_keycharacter varying(200)Text or composite key of the excluded source row. NULL = legacy_id identifies it.
reason_codecharacter varying(40)not nullWhy the row was not migrated: 'parent_deleted' = its parent row no longer exists in the source (Q21 orphans); 'retired_table' = the whole table is retired by decision (Q21 OrderTrn/OrderOrtho, Q18 offer50); 'unresolvable_reference' = a required reference cannot be resolved to any target row; 'duplicate_source_row' = an exact duplicate of a row already migrated; 'security_policy' = migrating it would create a security risk (U3, UserSessions live-looking tokens); 'approved_other' = another reason approved case by case (approval_reference required, explanation in details); 'pending_owner_decision' = held back until the owner decides (approval_reference stays NULL, so reconciliation reports the row as unexplained until approved).
approval_referencecharacter varying(200)Where the exclusion was approved: decision id (e.g. 'Q21', 'U3'), ticket or email reference. NULL = not yet approved; the row then counts as unexplained in reconciliation.
detailsjsonbnot nullSupporting facts as JSON (missing parent id, conflicting row id, note). Never PHI. · default '{}'::jsonb
created_attimestamp with time zonenot nullUTC instant the exclusion was recorded. · default now()
updated_attimestamp with time zonenot nullUTC instant of the last change (approval added). Maintained by trg_migration_exclusions__touch_updated_at. · default now()
constraints (6)

uq_migration_exclusions__run_id__legacy_rowUNIQUEUNIQUE NULLS NOT DISTINCT (run_id, legacy_table, legacy_id, legacy_key)A source row is excluded at most once per run, so re-running a step does not double-count; NULLS NOT DISTINCT makes a NULL id or key compare equal, and the ETL can upsert ON CONFLICT (run_id, legacy_table, legacy_id, legacy_key). Also serves the run_id FK.

One row per execution of the legacy-to-threeddx3 ETL (or a part of it): when it ran, against which source snapshot, with which code, and how it ended. audit.phi_access_log

PHIPIIAUDITV005 partitioned RANGE (occurred_at) · 25 rls forced · tenant isolation append-only 13 columns
Accounting of every read of patient identity (PHI) through the SECURITY DEFINER access functions (clinical.fn_get_patient_identity, clinical.fn_list_patient_identities, …): one row per patient per call, so "who saw this patient's identity, when and why" is one indexed query (HIPAA minimum-necessary and accounting of disclosures; GDPR access records). App and human roles cannot read clinical.patient_identities directly, so this log is complete for them. Written only by those functions; append-only (UPDATE, DELETE, TRUNCATE rejected); partitioned by month on occurred_at. Holds patient ids but no identity values. Contains PHI (the fact that a person accessed a given patient).

actor_role_idbigintAUDITiam.roles.id the person was acting in. No FK by design. NULL = no application role set (system process, direct database session). [AUDIT]

patient_idbigintPHInot nullclinical.patients.id whose identity was read. No FK by design: the access record must survive erasure or pseudonymisation of the patient (GDPR), and the writer function guarantees the id existed at read time. [PHI]
accessed_columnstext[]not nullIdentity fields returned, e.g. {full_name,date_of_birth}; lets an auditor check minimum-necessary use.
purposecharacter varying(100)not nullWhy the PHI was read, as passed by the caller (e.g. 'treatment', 'label_printing', 'billing', 'support'). Mandatory. The controlled vocabulary of purposes is TO CONFIRM with Compliance (Q9 disclosure matrix), so it is not a CHECK list yet.
function_namecharacter varying(130)not nullSchema-qualified access function that served the read, e.g. 'clinical.fn_get_patient_identity'; distinguishes single from bulk reads.
request_idcharacter varying(100)Correlation id of the HTTP request or job (app.request_id). NULL = no request id set (direct database session).
session_idcharacter varying(100)Identifier of the application login session (never the token). NULL = no application session (system process, direct database session).
client_addrinetPIIIP address of the end user's client as reported by the application. NULL = unknown (background job, local socket). [PII]

audit.reconciliation_results

V005 11 columns
Proof that a run migrated everything: one row per (run, legacy table, target table) with source = migrated + approved exclusions + unexplained, and status 'pass' only when unexplained is zero (design E10). Written by ETL stage 90. GLOBAL table (no tenant_id). Rows of a run are replaced (upsert on the unique key) when stage 90 is re-run within the same run; once the run is closed they are not changed.
columntypetags · constraintsmeaning
idbigintpkSurrogate key of the reconciliation row.
run_iduuidnot null on delete restrictRun being reconciled. FK to audit.migration_runs. · → audit.migration_runs
legacy_tablecharacter varying(80)not nullLegacy MySQL table counted, e.g. 'Orders'.
target_tablecharacter varying(160)not nullthreeddx3 table it was migrated into, schema-qualified, e.g. 'orders.orders'.
source_countbigintnot nullRows in the legacy table in the run's source snapshot.
migrated_countbigintnot nullSource rows represented in the target table (counted through audit.migration_id_map / legacy_id, so a source row that fans out into several target rows counts once).
excluded_countbigintnot nullSource rows in audit.migration_exclusions for this run and table with an approval_reference.
unexplained_countbigintnot nullsource_count - migrated_count - excluded_count. Positive = rows lost; negative = rows counted twice (both migrated and excluded, or a double load). Must be 0 to pass.
statuscharacter varying(20)not null'pass' = every source row is migrated or excluded with approval (unexplained_count = 0); 'fail' = unexplained rows remain.
notestextExplanation for reviewers (e.g. why a count differs). NULL = none.
created_attimestamp with time zonenot nullUTC instant the reconciliation was computed. · default now()
constraints (7)
namekinddefinitionrule
pk_reconciliation_resultsPRIMARY KEYPRIMARY KEY (id)Surrogate key of the result.
uq_reconciliation_results__run_id__legacy_table__target_tableUNIQUEUNIQUE (run_id, legacy_table, target_table)One reconciliation per source/target pair per run. Also serves the run_id FK.
fk_reconciliation_results__run_idFOREIGN KEYFOREIGN KEY (run_id) REFERENCES audit.migration_runs(run_id) ON DELETE RESTRICTEvery result belongs to a recorded run; a reconciled run cannot be deleted (RESTRICT, migration evidence).
ck_reconciliation_results__counts_non_negativeCHECKCHECK (((source_count >= 0) AND (migrated_count >= 0) AND (excluded_count >= 0)))Row counts are never negative (only the unexplained difference can be).
ck_reconciliation_results__pass_iff_zeroCHECKCHECK ((((status)::text = 'pass'::text) = (unexplained_count = 0)))A table passes if and only if no source row is unexplained (source = migrated + approved exclusions).
ck_reconciliation_results__statusCHECKCHECK (((status)::text = ANY ((ARRAY['pass'::character varying, 'fail'::character varying])::text[])))Reconciliation status is pass or fail.
ck_reconciliation_results__unexplained_arithmeticCHECKCHECK ((unexplained_count = ((source_count - migrated_count) - excluded_count)))Unexplained rows are exactly what source minus migrated minus excluded leaves; the database refuses a result whose arithmetic does not add up.

platform.client_event_logs

PHIPHI-RISKPIIV026 rls forced · tenant isolation append-only 13 columns
Bounded diagnostic events sent by the browser front end (legacy log-client.php, and PDF-generation failures, openapi gap G12): one row per accepted event. The endpoint rejects payloads above 8 KB and allow-lists the context it keeps; the CHECK enforces the same limit (D4 rule 19). Operational data, not audit evidence: rows are never updated, and old rows are purged by retention (period TO CONFIRM). page_path and payload may contain patient names typed into URLs or forms. Contains PHI-RISK.

finished_attimestamp with time zoneUTC instant the run ended. NULL = still queued/running, or a migrated sample that recorded no end time.
progress_percentsmallintProgress 0-100 reported by the job. NULL = the job does not report progress.
items_totalbigintNumber of items the run will process. NULL = unknown (legacy downloader samples record no total).
items_donebigintItems processed so far (bytes for the legacy downloader samples). NULL = not reported.
error_messagetextError text of a failed or timed-out run. NULL = no error.
metadatajsonbnot nullRun parameters and results (page measured, health-check result). Not filtered on. · default '{}'::jsonb
legacy_idbigintSource row id in the legacy table named by legacy_source. NULL = run recorded in threeddx3.
legacy_sourcecharacter varying(64)Legacy table the sample came from, e.g. 'daily_health_check'. NULL = run recorded in threeddx3.
legacy_keycharacter varying(200)Composite source key when legacy_id is not enough. NULL = not needed.

fn_ensure_monthly_partitions(p_parent regclass, p_months_ahead integer)integer
app_rw, owner
Creates any missing monthly partitions of a range-partitioned log table (audit.audit_log, audit.event_log, audit.phi_access_log, comms.email_logs) for this month and the next p_months_ahead months, with a comment on each. Run daily by a platform job; rows outside every partition fall into the DEFAULT partition and stay queryable. Returns how many partitions it created.
